About EnerVenue

EnerVenue is a Silicon Valley-based energy infrastructure company commercializing metal-hydrogen battery technology originally developed by NASA for the Hubble Space Telescope and the International Space Station. Founded in 2020 by Stanford Professor Yi Cui, EnerVenue adapts this proven aerospace chemistry for grid-scale terrestrial energy storage, delivering batteries with 30,000+ cycle lifetimes, inherent fire-safety, and a 30-year design life.

In 2026, EnerVenue closed a $300 million Series B extension and is well capitalized for growth. Funds are being deployed to build a high-volume manufacturing facility in Changzhou, China, targeting 250 MWh capacity by Q3 2026 and 1 GWh by 2027. EnerVenue has been named one of Time magazine's Top 10 US Green Technology Companies of 2025.

The Role

We are seeking a technically rigorous and customer-focused Energy Storage Applications Engineer to bridge the gap between our advanced energy storage technology and real-world deployment. This is a strategic, hands-on role critical to our mission. You will translate customer requirements into optimized system designs, validate performance across diverse use cases, and ensure our solutions deliver measurable value in the field. Acting as the technical backbone of the commercial process, you will support sales, marketing, product, and engineering teams with modeling, integration guidance, technical sales support, and application expertise.

This role covers EnerVenue's Middle East region and is based remotely in Saudi Arabia, working directly with utilities, developers, EPC contractors and industrial customers across the Kingdom and the wider GCC.

Key Responsibilities

Lead the Technical Pre-Sales Process:

Serve as the primary technical partner to Sales throughout the commercial lifecycle—from initial qualification through contract execution. Shape deal strategy by translating customer use cases, financial objectives, and operating constraints into technically optimized, commercially compelling storage solutions.

Translate Market Opportunities into Bankable Proposals:

·Lead technical discovery sessions to define duty cycles, performance guarantees, augmentation strategies, and integration requirements.

·Produce detailed technical proposals and bid packages, including system sizing, single-line diagrams, performance assumptions, and compliance documentation.

·Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Power Engineering, Energy Systems, or a related technical discipline.

·Demonstrated expertise designing multi-MW scale energy storage systems, with strong command of both DC and AC electrical design principles.

·High level of technical aptitude spanning from battery cell fundamentals through C&I and utility-scale battery systems.

·Working knowledge of grid connection and product compliance requirements applicable in Saudi Arabia and the wider GCC, including Saudi Electricity Company grid connection requirements and SASO / GSO conformity schemes.

·Solid understanding of how energy storage and PV projects are constructed, commissioned, and brought online.

Mandatory Core Competencies

jobs.excerpt: About PhaidraPhaidra is building the future of industrial automation.
jobs.description:
About Phaidra

Phaidra is building the future of industrial automation.

The world today is filled with static, monolithic infrastructure. Factories, power plants, buildings, etc. operate the same they've operated for decades — because the controls programming is hard-coded. Thousands of lines of rules and heuristics that define how the machines interact with each other. The result of all this hard-coding is that facilities are frozen in time, unable to adapt to their environment while their performance slowly degrades.

Phaidra creates AI-powered control systems for the industrial sector, enabling industrial facilities to automatically learn and improve over time. Specifically:

  • We use reinforcement learning algorithms to provide this intelligence, converting raw sensor data into high-value actions and decisions.
  • We focus on industrial applications, which tend to be well-sensorized with measurable KPIs — perfect for reinforcement learning.
  • We enable domain experts (our users) to configure the AI control systems (i.e. agents) without writing code. They define what they want their AI agents to do, and we do it for them.

Our team has a track record of applying AI to some of the toughest problems. From achieving superhuman performance with DeepMind's AlphaGo, to reducing the energy required to cool Google's Data Centers by 40%, we deeply understand AI and how to apply it in production for massive impact.

Phaidra’s ability to achieve its mission is determined by our ability to work together — as defined by our core values: Agency,Velocity, Craft, and Truth. We seek individuals who embody these values, as they are instrumental in ensuring our team consistently delivers excellence and fosters an engaging and supportive culture

Phaidra is based in the USA, but we are 100% remote with no physical office. We hire employees internationally with the help of our partner, OysterHR. Our team is currently located throughout the USA, Canada, UK, Sweden, Spain, Portugal, the Netherlands, Singapore, Australia, and India.

Who You Are

We are looking for a Staff Product Manager to lead one of the most important product bets at Phaidra: making Prism the connective data surface for the entire data center operation. It's the system operators trust for diagnostics and triage, and the layer executives rely on for operating intelligence across the site. Working closely with the CPO, you will shape and drive the strategy that extends Prism's reach from the floor to the boardroom.

You are bold and creative, with deep empathy for the operators on the floor who feel the pain first, and equal fluency with the executives who buy platforms. You spend time on-site and on calls with customers regularly, not just in research readouts, and you can tell me the last specific problem you heard from one. You think in systems and flywheels, not features. You are comfortable helping shape a big, opinionated bet and then sequencing the pragmatic steps that get there. You partner naturally with Engineering, AI, Design, and go-to-market, and you can hold a technical architecture discussion and a pricing-strategy discussion in the same afternoon.

**We are seeking teammates who are based in Eastern or Central time zones (US or Canada).

Responsibilities

You will partner with the CPO to develop and drive the product strategy and roadmap that establishes Prism as the agentic operating platform for the data center — spanning diagnostics, triage, and the broader intelligence layer operators and executives depend on.

Concretely, you will:

  • Work with the CPO to translate the platform vision into a sequenced, fundable roadmap, and drive it to delivery across teams.
  • Regularly visit and join calls with customers to see Prism in production and hear unfiltered feedback, not just what's escalated.
  • Translate floor-level customer pain into clear, high-quality product requirements, keeping teams close to real operator context.
  • Help drive expansion along two axes — connecting more of the data center’s operational and business systems, and advancing our insight & recommendations and supervised & autonomous control offerings.
  • Lead the delivery of key integrations that connect new systems into Prism, closing the loop from detection to diagnosis to action.
  • Partner with Engineering and Design to sequence and ship the platform capabilities that make broader, safer autonomy possible.
  • Support the expansion of Prism’s user base beyond the operations floor to new personas and buyers, including facilities and infrastructure leadership at hyperscale and neocloud operators, and partner with go-to-market and Finance on packaging and pricing.
  • Establish frameworks for prioritization, discovery, and risk mitigation; build high-quality product artifacts; coach and mentor other PMs, and help raise the standard for product practice — frameworks, artifacts, discovery rigor — across the team, not just within your own initiatives.
  • Own the metrics that define success in this role, including adoption across new systems and personas, progress along the insight-to-autonomy axis, and expansion revenue, and use them to guide prioritization and roadmap trade-offs.
  • Deeply understand the product architecture and participate actively in technical planning, so the strategy stays grounded in what the platform can actually do.
  • Help ensure alignment across teams by clearly communicating strategy, decisions, and trade-offs.

Key Qualifications

  • 8+ years of technical product management experience, including leading large, complex, cross-functional initiatives.
  • Comfortable spending significant time directly with customers or end users, and treats that time as core product work, not a distraction from it.
  • Track record of helping take a product from point solution toward platform — or contributing to a platform, integration, or data-surface product.
  • Exceptional ability to translate customer needs into strategic product direction and to sequence an ambitious vision into fundable steps.
  • Deep expertise in prioritization frameworks and product decision-making under uncertainty.
  • Strong technical acumen, including system architecture, integrations/APIs, and data platforms.
  • Ability to influence at all levels, including leadership, and to align teams on strategy, decisions, and trade-offs.
  • Experience mentoring and developing other product managers.
  • Excellent communication skills, including explaining complex ideas to audiences from the floor to the boardroom, in an all-remote setting.
  • Alignment with Phaidra's values: Agency, Velocity, Craft, & Truth.

Preferred Skills & Experience

  • Domain experience in data centers, critical infrastructure, industrial, or energy systems.
  • Experience with forward-deployed or services-led motions and turning them into platform revenue.
  • Familiarity with operational systems in this space, such as BMS/EPMS, CMMS, DCIM, or ITSM.
  • Experience productizing agentic AI or autonomous/closed-loop control.
  • Experience designing layered or usage-based B2B pricing, and familiarity with B2B sales and go-to-market.
  • Startup or high-growth experience with distributed/global teams.

Relevant Systems & Technologies

  • Prism platform and its knowledge base
  • Agentic control agents
  • BMS/EPMS telemetry
  • MQTT and other industrial communication protocols
  • Data center operational and business systems (e.g., CMMS, DCIM, ITSM)
  • GCP-based cloud stack

Onboarding

In your first 30 days…

  • Complete onboarding and immerse yourself in Prism, the strategy, and how a customer install works end-to-end today.
  • Spend time with operators to see the floor-level pain and the diagnostics/triage workflows Prism supports now.
  • Deeply understand our customer base and their major pain points.
  • Deeply understand your partners across Engineering, Design, Sales, and Leadership.

In your first 60 days…

  • Develop an informed point of view on roadmap sequencing and pressure-test it with the CPO, Engineering, and Design.
  • Take ownership of an early, high-leverage integration or capability, from requirements through delivery planning.
  • Join multiple live customer implementation and support calls.
  • Build the relationships across teams that you’ll need to drive a cross-functional bet.

In your first 90 days…

  • Partner with the CPO to publish a sequenced roadmap with clear near-term moves.
  • Have direct conversations with at least two major customer accounts to inform the roadmap and direction.
  • Land said high-leverage integration or expanded capability with a live customer deployment, thereby moving Prism one concrete step closer towards the platform direction.
  • Contribute to an initial pricing or packaging experiment with a friendly account.

General Interview Process

All of our interviews are held via Google Meet, and an active camera connection is required.

  1. Meeting with Operations (30 minutes) — You’ll meet with a member of the People Operations team to discuss your background and cover the formalities around your application.
  2. Hiring Manager interview (45 minutes) — You’ll discuss your experience and technical background with the hiring manager and have a chance to ask about the team and role.
  3. Product Manager Peer interview (45 minutes) — You’ll meet with one of our Product Managers to work through a case study.
  4. Cross Functional interview (60 minutes) — You’ll meet with our Creative Director and VP of Engineering to discuss prioritization, requirements, and cross-functional execution.
  5. Culture fit interview with one of Phaidra’s co-founders (30 minutes) — You’ll discuss alignment with Phaidra’s values and mutual cultural fit with one of our co-founders.

Base Salary

US Residents:

  • Tier 1 (Largest highest-cost metros): 180,800 USD - 248,600 USD
  • Tier 2 (Other major metros): 171,760 USD - 236,170 USD
  • Tier 3 (Mid-sized metro areas): 162,720 USD - 223,740 USD

In addition to base salary, this position is eligible for equity. Final salary will be determined based on several factors, including a candidate’s qualifications, skills, competencies, experience, expertise, education and location. In some cases, final compensation may fall outside the posted range. Salary ranges are regularly reviewed and may be adjusted in response to market trends.

Benefits & Perks

  • Fast-paced, team-oriented environment where your work directly shapes the company’s direction.
  • We are a 100% remote company.
  • Competitive compensation & meaningful equity.
  • Outsized responsibilities & professional development.
  • Training is foundational; functional, customer immersion, and development training.

  • Unlimited paid time off, with a required minimum of 20 days per year.
  • Paid parental leave (exact benefits vary by region).
  • Flexible stipends to support your workspace, well-being, and continued professional development.
  • Company MacBook.

Please note: Not all of Phaidra’s benefits and perks listed above apply to temporary employees such as interns.

On being Remote

We take a thoughtful and intentional approach to remote collaboration. Inspired by pioneers like GitLab, we embrace proven best practices to foster an exceptional remote work environment. Our culture is documentation-first, and we prioritize asynchronous communication to support focus and flexibility across time zones. While we value independence, we stay closely connected through tools like Slack and video conferencing. Weekly all-hands meetings help us align and build strong relationships, and we regularly host virtual team-building activities and social events to maintain a sense of camaraderie.

Contexto de negocio

Gestiona instituciones de educación superior en Perú y México, con procesos académicos y administrativos que atienden a estudiantes, docentes y áreas internas. La plataforma de aprendizaje virtual es clave para las clases en línea, y en periodos de matrícula, exámenes de admisión e inicio de clases no puede fallar.

Necesidad

Requiere incorporar un analista funcional que dé soporte de segundo nivel (L2) a la plataforma Blackboard y atienda nuevos requerimientos. Su rol es principalmente funcional, con conocimientos técnicos que le permitan atender incidentes, gestionar usuarios, cursos y matrículas, y apoyar los pases a producción.

Desafíos

La demanda de soporte es alta en los picos académicos y el equipo se organiza con rotación de fines de semana, mientras suma nuevas contrataciones. El perfil debe adaptarse rápido, ya que los primeros 15 a 21 días son de capacitación, y luego atender los tickets acumulados. Blackboard es un nicho, así que el cliente acepta experiencia en otros LMS y brindará la capacitación necesaria.

Oportunidad

Un analista funcional dedicado permitiría balancear la carga del equipo, mejorar los tiempos de respuesta y dar continuidad al servicio, ya que la posición está pensada con permanencia de largo plazo.

Valor del perfil

El perfil aporta experiencia en administración y soporte de plataformas de aprendizaje, atención de incidentes, pruebas funcionales (UAT) y reportes. Su incorporación contribuiría a reducir la carga del equipo en los picos académicos y a asegurar la disponibilidad de la plataforma para estudiantes y docentes.

Resumen del perfil

Profesional senior con experiencia en el soporte y la administración funcional de plataformas de aprendizaje (LMS), como Blackboard u otras similares. Cuenta con experiencia en la atención de incidentes y requerimientos, la gestión de usuarios, cursos, matrículas, roles y privilegios, y la ejecución de pruebas funcionales (UAT) previas al pase a producción. Tiene conocimientos técnicos en HTML, JavaScript y SQL, y manejo de reportes y analítica de datos. Se caracteriza por su orientación al servicio, su capacidad de respuesta en periodos de alta demanda y su facilidad para aprender nuevas herramientas del ecosistema de aprendizaje.

Funciones principales

  • Brindar soporte de segundo nivel (L2) a la plataforma de aprendizaje y atender nuevos requerimientos.
  • Atender incidentes, consultas administrativas y requerimientos: usuarios, cursos, matrículas, clonaciones, respaldos, roles y privilegios.
  • Administrar y mantener actualizada la plataforma, y realizar pruebas funcionales (UAT) en los ambientes de prueba antes del pase a producción.
  • Monitorear la salud de la plataforma y de las herramientas integradas, y escalar los problemas técnicos de forma oportuna.
  • Elaborar reportes e informes de la operación, y documentar los proyectos y las integraciones.

Requisitos generales

  • Bachiller en Ingeniería de Sistemas, Informática o carreras afines. El título es deseable.
  • Mínimo 3 años en posiciones similares de soporte o administración funcional de plataformas de aprendizaje (LMS).
  • Rol de enfoque funcional, con conocimientos técnicos. No supervisa personal.

Conocimientos indispensables

Funcional

  • Administración o soporte funcional de una plataforma de aprendizaje (Blackboard u otro LMS, por ejemplo Moodle, Canvas o D2L).
  • Atención de incidentes y requerimientos, y gestión de roles y privilegios.
  • Pruebas funcionales (UAT) y apoyo en pases a producción.
  • Analítica de datos, reportes y dominio avanzado de herramientas Office.

Técnico base

  • Conocimiento intermedio de HTML y JavaScript.

•SQL a nivel intermedio.

Se refuerzan en el proyecto

No se exige dominio previo. El equipo del cliente brinda apoyo y capacitación.

  • Blackboard en específico: el cliente brinda capacitación y grabaciones.
  • Herramientas del ecosistema de aprendizaje y proveedores LTI.

Conocimientos deseables

•Experiencia en el sector educativo.

  • Mantenimiento de ETLs y scripts de integración entre el sistema académico y la plataforma.
  • Conocimiento de C# y Python, e integración de servicios mediante APIs.
  • Conocimiento de metodologías de desarrollo y gestión de proyectos.

Job Description:

insightsoftware is seeking a Managing Counsel, Employment, Disputes & Litigation to lead the company's global disputes and litigation function within the Governance, Risk, Compliance & Disputes (“GRCD”) team. This role has enterprise-wide responsibility for managing all disputes and litigation matters including commercial, IP, contract, vendor, regulatory, employment, and other disputes across insightsoftware's global footprint of 40+ countries.

While the role carries a broad, general disputes mandate, the successful candidate will be an employment lawyer by trade and will continue to serve as the company's principal resource on employment-related disputes and litigation, working in close partnership with Human Resources. This role is a people-manager position, and reports directly to the SVP & Head, Global Legal Affairs & Compliance.

The ideal candidate is a confident, pragmatic litigator and people manager who can flex across dispute types and jurisdictions, build and lead a high-performing team, and calibrate risk across varied business contexts. This individual must be comfortable operating with significant independence while providing clear, actionable guidance to senior leadership.


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Disputes & Litigation Management

  • Own and manage the company's global disputes and litigation docket in its entirety, including commercial, contract, vendor, IP, regulatory, and employment-related matters.
  • Serve as the primary point of contact for incoming claims, demand letters, administrative charges, and civil litigation across all subject-matter areas; triage matters and determine case strategy.
  • Engage and oversee outside counsel across the full range of dispute types and jurisdictions; manage litigation budgets, billing guidelines, and outside counsel performance.
  • Evaluate and recommend settlement strategies in collaboration with senior leadership, business stakeholders, and GRCD teammates.
  • Manage employment-related disputes and litigation, including administrative charges (EEOC, state agencies, and international equivalents), demand letters, and civil litigation.
  • Maintain the enterprise disputes and litigation docket and provide regular status reporting to the SVP & Head, Global Legal Affairs & Compliance and other stakeholders as needed.
  • Oversee matter intake, legal hold administration, document collection, and discovery processes across active matters.
  • Draft and negotiate settlement, separation, and other resolution agreements across matter types.

Risk Management

  • Build, manage, and oversee scalable processes, playbooks, and reporting tools for disputes intake, escalation, and matter management as the docket grows.
  • Identify and assess legal and litigation risk across the business and work cross-functionally to develop mitigation strategies.
  • Support proactive compliance initiatives, including policy audits and training relevant to disputes and employment matters.

Employment Counseling & Advisory

  • Serve as the company's principal employment law advisor to Human Resources and business leaders on employment law matters across insightsoftware's international footprint, including the UK, EU member states, Canada, Australia, and other active jurisdictions, coordinating with regional and outside counsel as needed.
  • Advise on employee relations issues, including performance management, disciplinary actions, separations, and reductions in force.
  • Provide guidance on wage and hour compliance, leave management, accommodation requests, worker classification, and pay equity.
  • Review and advise on employment-related policies, handbooks, offer letters, employment agreements, and restrictive covenant agreements.
  • Partner with GRCD teammates and other stakeholders on governance and compliance matters that intersect with employment, including workplace investigations and ethics matters.
  • Monitor legislative and regulatory developments affecting litigation risk and the global workforce; proactively update internal stakeholders on changes with business impact.

Team Leadership & People Management

  • Directly manage and develop a team, setting priorities, providing coaching, and supporting professional growth.
  • Build team capacity and processes to support a growing and increasingly complex disputes caseload.
  • Foster a collaborative, high-accountability team culture consistent with insightsoftware's values.

QUALIFICATIONS

Required

  • Strong business judgment and ability to provide clear, practical legal advice in a fast-paced environment.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills; comfort presenting to senior leadership and the General Counsel.
  • Demonstrated flexibility and adaptability to manage a broad and evolving portfolio of dispute types across a global organization.
  • Experience managing commercial or IP litigation in addition to employment disputes.

Preferred

Azura Sankofa Advisory (ASA) is a lean global health advisory practice within Management Sciences for Health (MSH). We help governments strengthen and sustainably finance their health systems, and we work in support of government leadership rather than as a substitute for it. Our model is deliberately small: senior advisers, a flexible consultant roster, and the technical depth of MSH behind us.


The consultant will support ASA's mission to provide mission-focused global health consulting services that drive innovation, adaptiveness and sector change for governments and ministries. As we build our pipeline and prepare for our first funded engagements, we are looking for a senior consultant to provide part-time technical and business-development support during this period. The role's main priorities are winning work, producing strong technical proposals and concept notes, and building our consultant roster and delivery readiness. It also provides technical oversight of engagements once they are won. The consultant works closely with, and takes direction from, the Managing Director, who retains accountability for ASA's strategy, client relationships and final decisions.


Key Responsibilities

  • Business development. Help build and convert ASA's pipeline of government, donor and foundation opportunities, from qualification and capture planning through to submission, in coordination with MSH's business-development teams.
  • Proposals and concept notes. Lead the development of high-quality, country-owned concept notes and proposals, translating discussions with governments and partners into compelling technical offers, and drawing in expertise from ASA and across MSH.
  • Technical advisory. Provide senior technical expertise in support of government-led reform, across ASA's core focus areas (below).
  • Consultant roster and readiness. Help reorganise and strengthen the consultant roster, and provide recommendations regarding consultant qualifications, capabilities and staffing needs, so ASA can mobilise quickly and credibly when work is won.
  • Delivery oversight. Once engagements begin, support technical inception and quality, review key deliverables within delegated authority, and capture lessons learned, while the Managing Director holds client and strategic accountability.
  • Client and engagement support. Support the Managing Director on delivery planning and client engagement as time allows, and help draw MSH's technical expertise into ASA's proposals and work.

Technical Focus Areas

The consultant is expected to bring senior expertise in several of the following, applied in support of government leadership and country-owned reform:

  • Government advisory services and public-sector consulting.
  • Health financing and public financial management.
  • Health-systems strengthening, sustainability and transition.
  • Governance, accountability and regulatory compliance.
  • Government operations and reform, and organizational strategy.
  • Digital transformation as an enabler of health-system performance.

Terms

This is a remote role, with travel as required. Initial six months, renewable subject to need, performance and funding. Level of effort and daily rate to be agreed, against the relevant consultant band. This is an independent consultancy, not an employment position.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • At least 10 years' experience in global health, health financing, public financial management, governance, institutional strengthening or advisory services, including senior technical experience.
  • A strong track record of winning and delivering donor- and government-funded work, and of writing successful proposals, concept notes and investment cases.
  • Technical depth in one or more of ASA's core areas: health financing, public financial management, donor transition and co-financing, governance and accountability, or health-systems strengthening.
  • Experience supporting projects, programmes or clients across East and West Africa, with the ability to navigate diverse cultural, regulatory, business and political environments.
  • Credibility with senior government officials and funders, and a genuine commitment to country-led, government-owned reform.
  • Experience building consultant rosters, staffing models or proposal processes, and strong project-management discipline.
  • Excellent written and spoken English; additional language capabilities are desirable in regions where ASA operates. Comfortable working independently in an entrepreneurial, start-up environment, and able to travel when required.

DATA ANALYST

Department: Finance and Administration

JOB SUMMARY

One More Child is seeking to employ a full-time Data Analyst to support its mission of impacting vulnerable children and struggling families through the collection, integration, analysis, forecasting, and visualization of organizational data. The Data Analyst will bridge the gap between raw data and actionable intelligence by leveraging Microsoft Fabric's unified analytics platform to transform data into strategic insights that improve decision-making across fundraising, finance, program operations, and organizational leadership.

This position will be responsible for analyzing data from multiple sources, developing semantic data models, identifying trends and opportunities, conducting predictive analysis, and delivering interactive Power BI dashboards that translate data into meaningful business insights. The ideal candidate will possess strong analytical skills, advanced Microsoft Fabric and Power BI expertise, and the ability to communicate complex data findings to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND FUNCTIONS

  • Design and maintain interactive dashboards, reports, and scorecards using Power BI
  • Monitor Fabric data pipelines and datasets and extend semantic models.
  • Perform trend analysis, forecasting, and predictive analytics to support organizational planning and decision-making.
  • Maintain reliable reporting systems that include data from multiple legacy organizational systems and new data systems as needed; identify inaccurate or inconsistent data and work with appropriate departments to cleanse data and resolve underlying issues.
  • Utilize SQL, Power BI, and Fabric analytics tools to identify insights, opportunities, risks, and performance trends.
  • Develop and support machine learning and predictive models using Microsoft Fabric Data Science tools, Spark and/or Python.
  • Maintain and respond to automated monitoring, alerts, and reporting solutions using Microsoft Fabric capabilities.
  • Collaborate with business stakeholders to define reporting requirements, KPIs, and analytical needs.
  • Develop report wireframes, mockups, or prototypes to validate layout, metrics, filters, and user experience prior to dashboard development.
  • Present data-driven recommendations and insights to leadership and department teams.
  • Support data governance, data quality, security, and reporting best practices across the organization.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

REQUIRED EXPERIENCE AND QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience with Microsoft Fabric, including OneLake, and Data Warehouse.
  • Strong proficiency in SQL and experience querying large datasets.
  • Working knowledge of Python, Spark, or other data science and analytics tools.

jobs.title: Helpline Contact Center Supervisor
jobs.excerpt: Health Resources in Action, Inc.  (HRiA) is a non-profit organization working to improve and reimagine public health.
jobs.description:
Health Resources in Action, Inc. (HRiA) is a non-profit organization working to improve and reimagine public health. We connect, consult, and collaborate to solve complex challenges of access and equity in our health and social systems. Together with our partners, clients, and collaborators, we create actionable solutions so that all people can thrive.

In 1957, The Medical Foundation (TMF) was created to primarily fund biomedical research in Massachusetts. Since then, we’ve been on a journey of evolution. We changed our name to Health Resources in Action (HRiA) to reflect our impact in the field of public health. Today, HRiA works with individuals, organizations, and communities to drive a policy and systems change approach to advance health and racial equity.

HRiA seeks sustainable solutions for complex problems using an anti-racist approach. We aim to be adaptable and flexible in meeting clients and partners where they are, offering our decades of knowledge and resources to collectively realize our dream of equitable, sustainable health for all. The foundation of this work is centered on our values:

  • Health and racial equity by identifying and addressing the root causes of health inequities, intentionally working to shift narratives and power imbalances and disrupt all systems of oppression.
  • Leading with heart by demonstrating our passionate commitment to our work, continuously challenging ourselves with humility and vulnerability while pursuing and holding ourselves accountable to our mission.
  • Collaboration by intentionally and respectfully leading, partnering, and following to strengthen relationships, uplift different voices and build trust.
  • Innovation by driving toward new strategies, questioning norms, and continuously learning and evolving to support the needs of our clients and communities.

HRiA offers exciting, engaging, and challenging employment opportunities for facilitators, trainers, researchers, analysts, policy specialists, grant managers, and more. People come to HRiA because of our commitment to advancing health equity and inspiring work; they stay for our wonderful clients, partners, and dedicated and dynamic staff. With our growing portfolio of high-impact work, person-centered policies, and generous benefits, our team continually invests in making HRiA a great place to work. Our diverse staff of over 270 people hail from 30+ states, with a homebase in Boston’s Chinatown neighborhood.

As part of our Public Health Services, HRiA manages an extensive portfolio of behavioral health initiatives, including statewide substance use helplines in Vermont and Oregon and substance use and problem gambling helplines in Massachusetts and Illinois. The Illinois Helpline for Opioids and Other Substances (Illinois Department of Human Services, Division of Substance Use Prevention and Recovery) was launched in 2017, building upon our experience operating the MA Substance Use Helpline (Massachusetts Department of Public Health, Bureau of Substance Addiction Services) for over 23 years. HRiA launched the Vermont Helplink (Vermont Department of Health, Division of Substance Use Programs) in 2019. HRiA began operating the MA Problem Gambling Helpline (Massachusetts Department of Public Health, Office of Problem Gambling Services) in 2020 and the Illinois Problem Gambling Helpline (Illinois Department of Human Services, Division of Substance Use Prevention and Recovery) in 2022. In December 2023, HRiA launched the Oregon Recovery Center Hotline, now the Oregon Hopeline (Oregon Health Authority).

The Helpline contact center is the hub for the Helplines. Screening & Information Specialists (SIS) comprise most of the contact center team and respond to incoming Helpline inquiries. Four Contact Center Supervisors provide Helpline services and provide direct supervision to a portion of the SIS team. Three Masters-level Clinicians supervise a portion of the SIS, implement follow-up services, and provide additional coverage and support. Additional Helpline team members deliver and support program operations, marketing and communication, web management, and data analysis and management, supervision, and leadership. The larger team is overseen by the Managing Director, Behavioral Health.

To learn more about HRiA and our helplines, visit the following:

  • HRiA:
  • IL Problem Gambling Helpline:
  • MA Problem Gambling Helpline:
  • IL Helpline for Opioids and Other Substances:
  • VT Helplink: www.VTHelplink.org
  • MA Substance Use Helpline:
  • Oregon Hopeline:

Opportunity

We are seeking a full-time Helpline Contact Center Supervisor to join our team on the Oregon Recovery Center Hotline (Oregon Hopeline), Massachusetts Substance Use & Problem Gambling Helplines (MA Helpline), the Illinois Helpline for Opioids and Other Substances (IL Helpline), the Illinois Problem Gambling Helpline, and the Vermont Helplink (VT Helplink). This is an exciting opportunity to take on a newly developed position to support substance use treatment access across three states and supervise a diverse team of staff.

Position Description

We are seeking a full-time Helpline Contact Center Supervisor to join our team for the MA Helpines, the IL Helplines, and VT Helplink. We refer to these projects collectively as “the Helplines.” This is an exciting opportunity to support substance use treatment and problem gambling treatment access across three states and supervise a diverse team of staff.

The Contact Center Supervisors are responsible for handling incoming Helpline inquiries and providing supervisory support to the contact center team. A portion of their time is providing scheduled and as-needed Helpline coverage, in addition to our dedicated team of 22 Screening & Information Specialists (SIS). This includes responding to incoming calls, online chats, and SMS text messages from people seeking information about and help with accessing substance use and/or problem gambling services for themselves, a family member or friend, and/or a client. In this capacity, they assess Helpline users’ needs, determine the most appropriate substance use prevention, treatment, and/or recovery support service options, identify available options (through the Helplines’ databases), and refer callers to those services. They provide accurate information, education, support, and referrals in a non-judgmental, respectful, and culturally competent manner.

About half of their time, Contact Center Supervisors provide supervisory support to the SIS team. Each Supervisor acts as a shift supervisor for SIS while they are working. This includes monitoring SIS consumer interactions, consulting with SIS and intervening during difficult interactions, and addressing any urgent issues as well as supporting the social-emotional wellbeing of staff and fostering their skill-building and professional growth. The Contact Center Supervisor will provide on-going training to SIS through periodic in-service trainings on relevant topics and will assist in the onboarding of new SIS.

Each Supervisor also directly supervises up to six SIS team members. This includes providing bi-weekly supervision, processing timesheets, and assisting with schedule coordination. (SIS also receive regular, group-level supervision from one of our Clinicians.) Contact Center Supervisors are responsible for supporting contact center operations, including helping to coordinate a 24/7 coverage schedule, staffing, and technology needs. They are the liaisons between the contact center team and information technology (IT) support. The Contact Center Supervisor will also be called upon to contribute expertise to the development of policies, procedures, protocols, and curricula to support the Helplines, and may be engaged in providing this expertise to other HRiA teams and projects focused on substance use, problem gambling, and/or behavioral health equity.

This is a full-time, remote position with a salary range of $57,000 to $64,000 based on skills and experience. Supervisors will receive training to assess the needs of Helpline users, provide appropriate information and referrals to services, and engage with and motivate Helpline users to follow through on referrals. They will also receive training on Contact Center operations, supervision essentials, and addiction, screening, treatment services, and resources.

Benefits

HRiA offers strong benefits to its employees, including:

  • Competitive salaries
  • Health insurance
  • Retirement plan
  • Flexible summer hours
  • Vacation starting at four weeks
  • 13 paid holidays, and office closure at the end of December

Duties and Responsibilities

Management

  • Coordinate and implement projects related to contact center operations, including technology, equipment, onboarding & training, among others, as assigned.
  • Work with Helpline Management to coordinate Helpline staffing schedules to ensure continuous 24-hour staffing coverage.
  • Serve as liaison between SIS and other project and organizational teams, to ensure appropriate representation and facilitate team integration.
  • Supervise up to six SIS.
  • Participate in on-call rotation.

Project Work

  • Troubleshoot technical contact center issues, and serve as liaison to IT support.
  • Assist with coordination and implementation of onboarding and professional development activities.
  • Assess the needs of Helpline users by telephone, online chat, and SMS texting.
  • Provide appropriate information and referrals to substance use, problem gambling, and/or related services.
  • Engage and motivate Helpline users to follow through on referrals by using active listening and motivational interviewing techniques.
  • Obtain feedback on interactions with Helpline users.
  • Gather and record data from Helpline users in Helpline database.
  • Verify Helpline users’ insurance status, as applicable.
  • Escalate Helpline user interactions to Helpline Managers as needed.
  • Represent the Helpline at outreach events, meetings, and/or presentations as needed.

Thought Leadership

  • Continue to build and develop expertise in substance use disorders, problem gambling, and behavioral health equity.
  • Suggest ideas/improvements through participation in teams and committees.
  • Attend and actively participate in Helpline meetings and other activities to develop skills and make suggestions for project enhancements.

New Business Development

  • Maintain updated resume and bio for use in new business proposals.
  • Assist with technical components of new business proposals as needed.

Candidate Qualifications

  • Five years of related experience (lived or professional) in the fields of substance use, recovery, problem gambling, and/or harm reductions Services, and manage mentor bachelor’s degree in psychology, social work, human services, or related field in lieu of experience.
  • Certified Resource Specialist (through Inform USA) preferred or willingness to obtain certification (at HRiA expense) within one year of hire.
  • Demonstrated experience and ability to supervise staff, and provide appropriate guidance, feedback, mentorship, and support.
  • Experience in information and referral services, customer service, counseling, substance use, problem gambling, or human services required.
  • Ability to adapt to changes in work environment and expectations.
  • Customer/consumer focused with excellent interpersonal and communication skills.
  • Good computer skills and experience and/or ability to use online systems and databases.
  • Openness to information that may be different from personal views.
  • Willingness to work with consumers who may be ambivalent, resistant, impaired or have psychological disorders.
  • Must be open to providing information about a variety of treatment options and paths to recovery based on a caller’s needs.
  • Must be respectful of cultural differences and value diversity of thought, backgrounds, and perspectives.
  • Must have high ethical standards and a willingness to comply with professional expectations.
  • Demonstrated history of dependability needed.
  • Two years of sobriety requested for people in recovery.
  • Fluency in a language other than English (e.g., Spanish, Portuguese, Mandarin) is a plus.

Hours for this position will be non-traditional, requiring either early morning or late evening and weekend availability. The position includes weekend or overnight on-call duties. The Helplines are open 24 hours/day, 7 days/week, 365 days a year.

This description is intended to indicate the kinds of work duties that will be required in this position. It is not intended to limit, or in any way modify, the rights of any supervisor to assign, direct, and contract work of staff under his/her supervision. The use of a particular illustration describing duties shall not be held to exclude other duties, not mentioned, that are of a similar level or difficulty.

Procedure for Candidacy

HRiA is actively seeking to build a diverse and experienced staff. The organization encourages multiple perspectives and experiences, supports a multicultural environment, and strives to hire and retain a diverse work force that reflects the populations we work with and the communities where we work. Overview:

Intrax is a global organization dedicated to building a more inclusive and connected world through meaningful cultural exchange. Position Summary:

The Account Services Coordinator is a full-time, exempt position supporting the AmeriCamp program and Account Services team. This role partners closely with three Account Managers to support host camp recruitment and placement efforts by reviewing program documentation, coordinating hiring events, evaluating applicant submissions, and facilitating participant-to-camp matching.

The successful candidate will manage a high volume of host camp and participant records, ensuring accuracy, compliance, and timely completion of tasks in a fast-paced environment. During the summer season (May-September), the coordinator serves as a key support resource for participants and host camps, responding to inquiries, assisting with participant welfare and safety matters, resolving escalated issues, and participating in an emergency on-call rotation.

The ideal candidate is highly organized, detail-oriented, and adaptable, with strong communication skills and the ability to effectively prioritize competing responsibilities. Success in this role requires comfort working with databases and technology platforms, a commitment to accuracy, and the ability to quickly learn and navigate new systems and processes.

Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Review host camp documents (e.g., agreements, workers' compensation documents, job descriptions, and housing information etc.) for accuracy and completeness, following established protocols.

  • Ability to Learn Quickly – Open to feedback, embraces new systems and processes, and adapts quickly in an ever-changing environment.
  • Efficiency & Time Management – Works with a sense of urgency while maintaining accuracy, effectively prioritizing tasks, and meeting deadlines without sacrificing quality.
  • Positive, Team-Oriented Attitude – Communicates well with host camps and colleagues, collaborates effectively, is willing to support others, and contributes to a positive and solution-focused work environment.
  • Strong web-based technology and problem-solving skills.

jobs.description:
Overview

  • World Business Lenders (WBL) is a privately held portfolio lender specializing in real estate-secured business loans for underserved businesses. WBL operates with a fully remote, multinational workforce and an experienced executive leadership team.
  • Collateral spans U.S. markets, from primary metros to tertiary and rural locations, so this role must form defensible value opinions in markets the reviewer may not know firsthand.
  • Typical schedule is 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM Eastern Time, Monday through Friday, with additional hours as committee timing and business needs require.

What You'll Be Doing (Core Responsibilities)

  • Review appraisals, evaluations, BPOs, and CMA’s for accuracy, methodology, and compliance with USPAP and the Interagency Appraisal and Evaluation Guidelines; return deficient reports for correction.
  • Test value conclusions against independent market evidence (MLS, public records, CoStar, broker reports) in any U.S. market.
  • Flag weak comparables, unsupported adjustments, stale data, math errors, and unreasonable extraordinary assumptions or hypothetical conditions.
  • Analyze income property: rent rolls, operating expenses, NOI, cap rates, and discounted cash flow (DCF) assumptions.
  • On construction and development loans, compare budgets, draws, and completion status against as-complete value conclusions.
  • Recommend a value for each relevant premise (as-is, as-complete, as-stabilized, disposition) suited to the loan’s stage: origination, performing, default, workout, or REO.
  • Write concise findings and present recommendations for Investment, Asset Resolution, and Initial Credit Review.
  • Recommend added work when information is insufficient: new appraisal, inspection, environmental, or engineering report.

Requirements

  • Education
    • Bachelor’s degree in real estate, finance, economics, business, or a related field.
  • Required Experience
    • 5+ years in appraisal, appraisal review, collateral valuation, underwriting, or asset management, the majority on commercial collateral.
    • Hands-on commercial and income-property valuation or review experience; residential review experience is a plus.
    • Working knowledge of the sales comparison, income, and cost approaches, and of USPAP.
    • Experience with distressed, foreclosed, or REO property.
    • Strong Excel, writing, and presentation skills, and the confidence to challenge unsupported conclusions.
  • Preferred Background / Industry Experience
    • State Certified General or Certified Residential appraiser credential or progress toward Certified General.
    • A professional valuation designation, or active candidacy for one, such as:
      • AI-GRS (General Review Specialist, Appraisal Institute), the designation focused on commercial appraisal review
      • MAI (Appraisal Institute), for commercial and income-producing property
      • MRICS (Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors)
      • ASA (American Society of Appraisers), Real Property
      • CCIM (CCIM Institute), for commercial investment analysis
      • ARA (American Society of Farm Managers and Rural Appraisers), for rural and agricultural property
      • AI-RRS or SRA (Appraisal Institute), for residential review and valuation
      • Commercial appraisal review experience at a bank, portfolio lender, or private credit fund.
    • Familiarity with construction and development projects and the cash flow-based analysis used to value them.

Key Performance Measures

    • Accuracy of recommended values against subsequent sales and recoveries
    • Material deficiencies caught before funding, workout, or disposition decisions
    • Review turnaround time and consistency with WBL standards
    • Quality of written findings and committee presentations
    • Growth into independent review of complex commercial and development assets

Remote Work Requirements

  • Stable, reliable internet connection.
  • Professional and dedicated remote working environment.

🏖️ Benefits include medical, dental, vision, life, and disability coverage; a 401(k) with company match; and paid holidays and paid time off (PTO).

Time Zone and Schedule:

Chemistry Fit: We have a unique and fun culture—we laugh, press in, work hard, and jump in to figure things out. Fitting into the team chemistry is essential.

Energy & Enthusiasm: This person must bring joy and passion for work to the job. Encouraging and spurring on others on the mission while being self-motivated and positive is essential.

Multitasking: This is not a steady-state or static environment. Workflow will cycle, and interruptions are normal, so this person must be able to juggle and adjust on the fly.

Project Management: While multitasking, this person must be able to keep an eye on deadlines and critical dependencies, working to preserve them or source support proactively.

Do not conform to the pattern of this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind. Then you will be able to test and approve what God’s will is—his good, pleasing and perfect will. Romans 12:2

jobs.excerpt: Are you looking to make an impactful difference in your work, yourself, and your community?
jobs.description:
Are you looking to make an impactful difference in your work, yourself, and your community? Why settle for just a job when you can land a career? At ICW Group, we are hiring team members who are ready to use their skills, curiosity, and drive to be part of our journey as we strive to transform the insurance carrier space. We're proud to be in business for over 50 years, and its change agents like yourself that will help us continue to deliver our mission to create the best insurance experience possible.


Headquartered in San Diego with regional offices located throughout the United States, ICW Group has been named for the twelfth consecutive year in a row and for the 20th time overall as a Top 50 performing P&C organization offering the stability of a large, profitable and growing company combined with a focus on all things people. It's our team members who make us an employer of choice and the vibrant company we are today. We strive to make both our internal and external communities better everyday! Learn more about why you want to be here!


PURPOSE OF THE JOB

The purpose of this job is to handle all aspects of workers’ compensation cases with varying degrees of complexity and to provide other litigation and claim legal advice and services to all areas of the company. This role exists to provide high quality, proactive case handling utilizing legal expertise and litigation skills to independently handle a caseload of high exposure cases and complex litigation matters and deliver optimal results for ICW Group.


ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Provides litigation services and is responsible for all aspects of assigned Workers’ Compensation matters.

  • Manages the entire legal process, from investigation and discovery though trial prep and court proceedings, depositions, site inspections, court hearings, trials, etc. and negotiating settlements as required.
  • Litigates workers’ compensation cases in California before all state and federal courts, administrative boards, and other court proceedings.
  • Represents ICW Group, its related entities and insureds before administrative boards, state and federal courts, Court of Appeal, and the California Supreme Court.
  • Handles premium audit disputes before administrative boards or other court proceedings.
  • Assists in subpoenas and other third-party discovery.
  • Analyzes complex legal and factual issues; conducts extensive, well-reasoned legal research, as necessary; independently develop and present defense strategies on behalf of ICW Group.
  • Responsible for the prompt, efficient and effective disposition of assigned cases.

Provides accurate legal analysis and strategy recommendations to clients and claims personnel.

  • Assists in analyzing, reviewing, and distributing information on new legislation, regulations, court decisions and proceedings.
  • Provides strategic legal advice, recommendation, and implementation of clear, cost-effective, and efficient plans of action.
  • Delivers ongoing quality assessments of the law and facts and recommendations for timely resolution.
  • Analyzes all referrals from claims and determines need for outside investigation or other information from the insured or others.
  • Provides effective and timely communications, information, legal advice, and other services to clients and claims professionals on legal and factual issues.
  • Develops appropriate legal strategies for all stages of litigation and shares them with claims personnel and clients.

Provides leadership through mentoring other attorneys and legal support staff.

  • Directs paralegals and other legal department staff in their duties and responsibilities in handling cases.
  • Ensures timely filing of all pleadings and motions or other documents with the court or administrative broads.
  • Builds and fosters internal and external client relationships with a customer-centric focus.
  • Adheres to all ICW Group’s policies and procedures and the California Rules of Professional Conduct.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

This role does not have direct supervisory responsibilities. Position will direct the work of support staff, which may include assistants and paralegals, in accordance with company policies and applicable laws, including the California Rules of Professional Conduct. These responsibilities include planning, assigning, and directing work; review, revise and approve legal documents; delegate tasks to the appropriate staff member; train, coach, and mentor, as appropriate, support staff to ensure the delivery of quality legal services.


EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

Bachelor’s degree from four-year college or university required. Juris Doctorate (JD) from an accredited law school required. Minimum 7-10 years of workers’ compensation litigation experience or equivalent combination of education and experience required.


CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS

Licensed and in good standing with the State Bar of California required, with no history of public or private reprisals.


KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS

Expert knowledge in litigating California workers’ compensation matters with trial experience and prior experience handling cases with varying degrees of complexity. Must have a deep understanding of workers’ compensation administrative rules, procedures, laws, and statutes. Familiarity with business legal principles and practices is necessary, including knowledge of billing practices and procedures. Demonstrated experience in working independently under minimal supervision, maintaining a strong work ethic, and exercising initiative. Ability to communicate effectively with external and internal clients both verbally and in writing. Ability to read, analyze, and interpret technical documents, legal materials of all types, and medical records. Strong negotiation and communication skills. Ability to respond to inquiries, issues, or questions from internal and external clients, businesses, and members of the State Bar or Judiciary, and regulatory agencies, including effectively responding to the most sensitive inquiries or concerns. Ability to effectively present information, verbally and in writing to clients, claims personnel, management, mediators, arbitrators, judges, juries, and members of the public. Proficient use of a personal computer and skills with Microsoft Word, Excel, Outlook, Adobe, and PowerPoint. Ability to learn various proprietary computer applications. Ability to work with mathematical concepts and apply concepts such as fractions, percentages, ratios, and algebra and geometry to practical situations. Ability to combine pieces of information to form general rules or conclusions and problem-solve. Ability to define legal issues, collect necessary data, establish facts, draw legal conclusions, and implement a strategic legal resolution. Expert at time management skills, appropriate delegation of activities and the ability to manage multiple legal matters at one time.


PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

Office environment – no specific or unusual physical or environmental demands and employees are regularly required to sit, walk, stand, talk, and hear.


WORK ENVIRONMENT

This position operates in an office and court environment and requires frequent use of a computer, telephone, copier, scanner, and other standard office equipment. The position requires traveling to various court locations as well as other business locations.


We are currently not offering employment sponsorship for this opportunity


The current range for this position is

$137,617.39 - $232,082.34

This range is exclusive of fringe benefits and potential bonuses. If hired at ICW Group, your final base salary compensation will be determined by factors unique to each candidate, including experience, education and the location of the role and considers employees performing substantially similar work.


WHY JOIN ICW GROUP?

  • Challenging work and the ability to make a difference
  • You will have a voice and feel a sense of belonging
  • We offer a competitive benefits package, with generous medical, dental, and vision plans as well as 401K retirement plans and company match
  • Bonus potential for all positions
  • Paid Time Off
  • Paid holidays throughout the calendar year
  • Want to continue learning? We’ll support you 100%

ICW Group is committed to creating a diverse environment and is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. ICW Group will not discriminate against an applicant or employee on the basis of race, color, religion, national origin, ancestry, sex/gender, age, physical or mental disability, military or veteran status, genetic information, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, marital status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state or local law.

jobs.title: Telehealth Registered Dietitian
jobs.excerpt: Simplex Health is seeking a Registered Dietitian (RD/RDN) to provide telehealth outpatient nutrition counseling in an integrative/functional nutrition setting.
jobs.description:
Simplex Health is seeking a Registered Dietitian (RD/RDN) to provide telehealth outpatient nutrition counseling in an integrative/functional nutrition setting. This is a PRN (as-needed) role requiring a minimum of 12 hours of weekly availability, with the opportunity to offer additional hours if desired. The ideal candidate has experience in clinical or outpatient nutrition counseling, is licensed (or eligible for licensure) in Pennsylvania, and is passionate about delivering personalized, root-cause care to support long-term health outcomes.

Our Mission: Radically improve the health of Humankind-one person, one appointment, one connection at a time.

At Simplex Health, we do things differently. Our insurance-funded medical nutrition therapy goes beyond symptom management to improve — and in many cases reverse — chronic conditions. We partner with hospitals, healthcare practices, and individuals to provide personalized, root-cause nutrition care across a wide range of conditions, including metabolic health, digestive disorders, hormonal imbalances, and chronic disease.

Our approach is grounded in prevention, root-cause resolution, and sustainable lifestyle change, supporting patients throughout their health journey. Through a fully virtual, telehealth model, we meet patients where they are, delivering accessible, high-quality care.

Our evidence-based, progressive nutrition interventions are tailored to each patient’s unique biochemistry. Through nutrition counseling, education, and health coaching, we empower patients to improve their health, build lasting habits, and achieve meaningful, long-term outcomes.

Role Details:

  • Location: Telehealth
  • Reports to: Clinical Manager
  • Schedule: PRN / flexible with consistent weekly availability
  • Compensation: $54 to $59 hourly

You love helping people heal. You just don’t love doing it all alone.

If you’ve ever run (or dreamed of running) your own private practice, you know what it takes — the marketing, the scheduling, the billing, the insurance headaches, the empty calendar days, the tech issues, the isolation…

At Simplex Health, you get the best parts of private practice — the autonomy, the flexibility, the deep 1:1 relationships with patients — without the burnout or business stress.

Here, you get to focus on what you do best: helping patients transform their health through integrative and functional nutrition.

What we are looking for

We’re seeking mission-driven dietitians (RD/RDN) who:

  • Are passionate about integrative and functional nutrition
  • Thrive in a collaborative, growth-minded environment
  • Have at least 2 years of experience in outpatient or clinical care
  • Hold current registration with CDR
  • Are credentialed or open to being credentialed with insurance companies
  • Minimum of 12 hours of weekly availability required, with flexibility and opportunity to increase hours over time based on your preferences and schedule
  • Want to spend more time with patients and less time running a business
  • To avoid conflicts of interest, candidates should not maintain an active private practice or independent nutrition counseling business

Preferred:

  • Availability for evening appointments strongly preferred to meet patient demand, with flexibility based on individual scheduling needs.
  • CDCES (Certified Diabetes Care and Education Specialist) strongly preferred
  • IFNA Certified (IFNCP credential a plus); candidates actively enrolled in IFNA training welcome

PA license and completion of major insurance credentialing required before start; this process may take 3–6 months.

Role Responsibilities (including but not limited to):

  • Provide telehealth medical nutrition therapy using a functional and integrative approach
  • Implement Simplex Health protocols, tools, and educational materials in patient care
  • Assess the nutritional health of patients/clients and develop personalized, root-cause care plans
  • Create and modify individualized nutrition interventions based on patient needs and goals
  • Document all new and follow-up appointments in the Healthie platform with strong attention to detail
  • Respond to patient communications in a timely, professional, and supportive manner
  • Collaborate with team members through case discussions, meetings, and shared learning opportunities
  • Communicate openly and effectively to resolve work-related issues and support team outcomes
  • Contribute to a positive, collaborative team environment and ongoing clinical initiatives
  • Adhere to all company policies, procedures, and clinical standards
  • Stay current with emerging research and best practices in nutrition and health
  • Manage a full and consistent patient caseload, ensuring timely follow-ups, continuity of care, and optimal patient outcomes
  • Maintain a minimum of 12 hours of weekly availability, with opportunity to grow into a higher-hour or full-time schedule

What to Expect
At Simplex Health, you’ll have access to:

  • Structured onboarding and training
  • Regular case reviews and clinical collaboration
  • Real-time support via team chat and peer connection
  • Team meetings and shared learning opportunities
  • Opportunities to contribute to committees, resources, and clinical initiatives
  • Credentialing: If you’re not yet in-network, our team fully manages the insurance credentialing process on your behalf, including covering all associated fees and handling the paperwork.

Benefits

  • Flexible Scheduling: Set your availability with the ability to build and adjust your schedule based on your preferences and patient demand
  • Supplement Commissions: Earn 12.5% of MSRP on supplements purchased through Fullscript. Commissions are paid quarterly and can meaningfully increase your overall earnings based on patient engagement.
  • Performance-Based Bonus Opportunities: Earn additional income based on patient retention and face-to-face care time.
  • Paid Time Off (PTO): Accrue 1 hour of PTO for every 12 hours of patient care, supporting flexibility and time away as you work.
  • Discretionary Holiday Break: Office closed between Christmas and New Year’s — guaranteed time off from patient appointments & administrative work
  • Fitness Allowance: Partial reimbursement for gym memberships, fitness classes, or wellness activities
  • Simplex Wellness on Demand: Free access to virtual fitness programs

Key Intangible Characteristics of the Ideal Candidate:

Called: A passion for our mission and a sense that this role and company are a strong fit for the blessings of your gifts, talents, passions, and experiences.. Must be mission-motivated with a resolve to overcome obstacles, anchored in a sense of purpose in this work.

Servant Leadership: Nobody is above any task, and we are all here to serve others. Every customer—internal or external—needs help, and the most powerful way to lead will be to serve.

Learning and Adaptive: As a startup with a big mission, new systems, technology, and situational adaptability are expected. This person must have an appetite for learning and skill improvement.

Grit, Resourcefulness & Entrepreneurial Spirit: Not everything will have a pre-planned solution. This person will have to be resourceful in figuring things out, resist feeling overwhelmed, and be willing to roll up their sleeves to make things happen. This person will have to have an open mind and good resolve, whether it’s looping in other people, finding answers online, or seeking best practices.

Organizational Skills: Being or becoming a constant organizational force. It will require a capacity for being open to change, discerning better processes, and prioritizing for improved outcomes.

Chemistry Fit: We have a unique and fun culture—we laugh, press in, work hard, and jump in to figure things out. Fitting into the team chemistry is essential.

High Character: We operate with a high trust culture. Personal values must fuel our work. Integrity, honesty, compassion, reconciliation, and diligence are all things this person must possess to flourish.

Energy & Enthusiasm: This person must bring joy and passion for work to the job. Encouraging and spurring on others on the mission while being self-motivated and positive is essential.

Multitasking: This is not a steady-state or static environment. Workflow will cycle, and interruptions are normal, so this person must be able to juggle and adjust on the fly.

Project Management: While multitasking, this person must be able to keep an eye on deadlines and critical dependencies, working to preserve them or source support proactively.

🌟 Why Dietitians Choose Simplex Health

Because great clinicians deserve great support.

🧾 We Handle Credentialing & Licensing
We cover insurance credentialing costs and reimburse for out-of-state license fees.

🎓 CEU Reimbursement
We invest in your professional growth and continued learning.

💻 Technology Reimbursement
Support for the tools you need to work efficiently and effectively.

💲 Recruitment Thank You Bonus
Bonus for any referrals hired by Simplex Health who stay at least 90 days

📋 Consistent Referrals & Quality Resources
A steady patient flow and high-quality patient-facing materials to support your care.

👥 Helpful Support Team & Quick Response Times
From scheduling to tech help, our support staff makes your day run smoother.

🌿 Approachable Leadership & Collaborative Culture
Leaders who listen, and a clinical community that truly supports one another.

🤝 Opportunities Beyond Patient Care
Get involved with social media, engagement projects, or hosting lunch & learns.

🌎 Broad Range of Clients, Deep Skill Development
Grow your counseling skills and confidence across a variety of cases.

💞 Strong Sense of Community
Even in a virtual environment, you’ll feel connected, encouraged, and supported.

If you’ve ever wished you could combine the freedom of private practice with the camaraderie and stability of a larger organization, this is where you belong.

Apply today and rediscover the joy of patient care without the grind of running a business.

Simplex Health Core Values:

Simplex Health strives to embody the following values and to apply them to every aspect of how we run our business, including how we interact with each other as teammates and leaders. These values also apply to how we interact with and continue to inspire our clients and strategic partners:

We Inspire Each Other
You are an important part of our team and together we make a collective intention to uplift and commit to one another. Through cultivating genuine, transparent, relationships, we create an environment that encourages individuals to dream big, take risks, and be bold. We aim to inspire and commit to everyone we touch. This sense of commitment and care sets the stage for a culture of accountability, where we hold ourselves and each other to the same high standards, taking the ownership necessary for achieving our goals.
Therefore encourage one another and build each other up, just as in fact you are doing.
1 Thessalonians 5:11

We Always Learn and Grow
We at Simplex Health strive to be continual learners and to expand our abilities as people and as an organization. We educate ourselves, remain curious, and use evidence-based research to challenge our current understanding. We see mistakes and failure as great teachers and learning opportunities. When we stay engaged in the world with a growth mindset, it creates the right environment for us to thrive and make a meaningful impact on each other and on the world.
Let the wise hear and increase in learning, and the one who understands obtain guidance.
Proverbs 1:5

We Think Big Picture What we do day in, day out, how we do it, and the decisions we make- shape who we are as a people and as a company. The details are super important, AND should always be guided by our wide perspective and an understanding of how we are impacting each other, our clients, and our business. Before making any major decision, ask yourself:

• Does it help us grow? How?

• Does it answer “how are we different and why should you care?”
• Is what I’m working on duplicatable and transferable (ie can I duplicate it and apply to other situations)? How?
• Does it challenge the status quo?
• Does it inspire?
• Does it tightly align with and advance our mission? How?
• Can it be more humanized and relatable?
• Does it unite us? How?
• Does it solve a problem? How?
Now we see things imperfectly, like puzzling reflections in a mirror, but then we will see everything with perfect clarity. All that I know now is partial and incomplete, but then I will know everything completely, just as God now knows me completely.
I Corinthians 13:12

We Challenge the Status Quo:
We are inquisitive by nature. We are courageous! We are not afraid to go against the grain in our search for truth. We always question conventional wisdom- it’s how Simplex Health started- it’s what we do.
Do not conform to the pattern of this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind. Then you will be able to test and approve what God’s will is—his good, pleasing and perfect will. Romans 12:2

We Cultivate Health and Vitality:
Being alive in a body is an incredible, temporary experience. Even though at times we feel pain and face challenges, our next breath is not guaranteed and is a HUGE gift. We experience EVERYTHING through our bodies, including thoughts, emotions, spirit, and our inspiration. We see health and vitality as the foundation for living a life that is happy, fulfilled, present, and productive.
Dear friend, I pray that you may enjoy good health and that all may go well with you, even as your soul is getting along well.
3 John 1:2

We Embody Integrity:
We communicate with transparency and face conflict head-on. We do this with the understanding that we respect each other and recognize that we are on the same team working toward a unified noble mission with shared goals. We don’t compromise our morals or integrity no matter the context. When challenging scenarios arise, we approach them with honesty and trust that we are all holding the highest intentions, are committed to our values, and are making best efforts.
Do to others as you would have them do to you.
Luke 6:31

We Simplify the Complicated:
We believe that complex problems don’t always require complex solutions. By simplifying the complicated and offering digestible, scalable solutions, we can pay more attention to the things that matter most. Simplicity- it’s the word that inspired our name - we make cultivating health and vitality simple.
Do not be anxious about anything, but in everything by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known to God.
Philippians 4:6
