jobs.description:
We're looking for a B2B Software Sales Representative to be the first dedicated sales hire at a fast-growing B2B SaaS company serving field service and operations businesses. You will own the entire sales funnel end to end — from inbound lead response and outbound prospecting through discovery, demo, proposal, and close. This is not an appointment-setting role.

You will be the single sales seat reporting directly to the founder. That means full ownership of pipeline, CRM hygiene, SOP execution, and closing — software subscriptions and professional services packages both. If you are a proven closer who can work independently, follow a documented process without being micromanaged, and take genuine ownership of revenue outcomes in an early-stage environment, this role is a strong fit.

Why You'll Want to Join

  • You will be paid in USD (bi-monthly: every 15th and 30th)
  • Paid Time Off in accordance with company policy
  • Observance of Holidays per company guidelines
  • 100% remote setup so you can work wherever you're most productive
  • This role requires availability during US business hours
  • Additional financial incentives for professional services closings
  • First sales hire with direct access to the founder and real influence over how the sales function is built
  • High-ownership role with direct impact on revenue and company growth

What You'll Work On

Full-Funnel Sales Ownership

  • Own the complete sales cycle from research and outreach through qualification, demo, proposal, close, and handoff to onboarding
  • Engage inbound leads immediately via call, email, and SMS as defined in the sales SOP — speed to lead is a hard expectation
  • Run structured discovery conversations covering pain, current tools, decision process, timeline, and budget signals
  • Lead product demos with support from the customer success team
  • Send proposals and quotes, chase signatures, and confirm kickoff details for every won deal
  • Close both software subscription plans and professional services and onboarding packages

Outbound Prospecting

  • Research target accounts and build call lists proactively
  • Conduct cold and warm outbound calls and emails to book meetings
  • Maintain a consistent outbound motion alongside inbound lead response

CRM and Pipeline Management

  • Own CRM management day to day including pipeline stages, fields, tags, sequences, and logging every touch
  • Keep pipeline hygiene tight with next steps, close dates, and notes always current and accurate
  • Maintain CRM and SOP usage at a standard the founder can trust without checking behind you

Reporting and Process Contribution

  • Provide light weekly reporting covering activity, pipeline, wins, losses, and blockers
  • Feed the product and marketing teams with real call insights including ICP feedback, common objections, and feature requests
  • Help refine scripts, talk tracks, and ICP definitions as the sales function scales from founder-led to team-led
  • Handle objections and negotiate within approved pricing guidelines, escalating edge cases to leadership

What You Bring

  • Proven experience closing or strongly contributing to closing B2B software or high-consideration sales — not appointment setting only
  • Excellent spoken English with the confidence and presence to lead live demos and discovery calls independently
  • Self-directed and high ownership mindset — comfortable being the only sales person reporting directly to a founder
  • Strong CRM discipline with the ability to follow a documented sales SOP consistently without being reminded
  • Reliable availability during US business hours with strong outbound phone skills

Nice to Have

  • Spanish language skills for communicating with Spanish-speaking clients
  • Experience selling to SMB, field service, or trade service businesses
  • Prior experience as an early or first sales hire at a startup
  • Familiarity with CRM tools such as HubSpot or GoHighLevel

How to Apply

Please include:

  1. Your updated resume
  2. A short Loom video (1 to 2 minutes) introducing yourself, describing your full-cycle B2B sales experience, and walking through a deal you owned from first contact through close — including how you ran discovery and handled objections along the way

Only candidates who submit a Loom video will be moved to the next step of the hiring process.

If you are a proven closer who takes full ownership of your pipeline, follows process without being micromanaged, and wants to be the person who builds the sales function from the ground up at an early-stage SaaS company, this role gives you the autonomy and the direct impact to do your best work.

Application Process Overview

Our comprehensive selection process ensures we find the right fit for both you and our clients:

  1. Initial Application - Submit your application and complete our prequalifying questions
  2. Video Introduction - Record an video introduction to showcase your communication skills and work experience
  3. Role-Specific Assessment - Complete a homework assignment tailored to the position (if applicable)
  4. Recruitment Interview - Initial screening with our talent team
  5. Executive Interview - Meet with senior leadership to discuss role alignment
  6. Client Interview - Final interview with the client team you'd be supporting
  7. Background & Reference Check - Professional reference verification
  8. Job Offer - Successful candidates receive a formal offer to join the team

Each stage is designed to evaluate your fit for the role while giving you insights into our company culture and expectations. We'll keep you informed throughout the process and provide feedback at each step.

jobs.description:
Department:

104275 FILSPARI Global Strategy

Location:

San Diego, USA- Remote

Be a part of a global team that is inspired to make a difference in the lives of people living with rare disease.

At Travere Therapeutics, we recognize that our exceptional employees are vital to our success. We are a dedicated team focused on meeting the unique needs of rare patients. Our work is rewarding – both professionally and personally – because we are making a difference. We are passionate about what we do.

We are seeking talented individuals who will thrive in our collaborative, diverse, fast-paced environment and share in our mission – to identify, develop and deliver life-changing therapies to people living with rare disease. We stick by our values centered on patients, courage, community, and collaboration to pursue our vision of becoming a leading biopharmaceutical company dedicated to the delivery of innovation and hope to patients in the global rare disease community.

At Travere Therapeutics, we are in rare for life. We continue to courageously forge new paths as we move toward a common goal of elevating science and service for rare patients.

Position Summary


The Executive Director, Health Economics & Outcomes Research (HEOR) will provide strategic leadership for the development and execution of health economics, outcomes research, real-world evidence, patient-reported outcomes and evidence synthesis strategies across Travere Therapeutics’ nephrology portfolio, including FILSPARI® (sparsentan), civorebrutinib, and future pipeline assets.

This individual will be responsible for developing an integrated evidence strategy that demonstrates the clinical, humanistic, and economic value of Travere’s therapies throughout the product lifecycle. The Executive Director will partner closely with Medical Affairs, Clinical Development, Market Access, Commercial, Regulatory Affairs, Biostatistics, and other cross-functional partners to identify evidence needs and ensure generation of high-quality data that supports scientific exchange, patient access, clinical development, and future value demonstration.

The Executive Director will serve as the senior HEOR expert for the Nephrology Franchise and will help shape the long-range evidence strategy for marketed and development-stage assets.

Responsibilities:


  • Develop and lead the HEOR and value evidence strategy across Travere’s nephrology portfolio, including FILSPARI, civorebrutinib, and future pipeline assets.
  • Develop integrated evidence-generation plans that address clinical, economic, humanistic, and healthcare decision-maker evidence needs across the product lifecycle.
  • Partner closely with Clinical Development, Medical Affairs, Market Access, Regulatory, and Biostatistics to identify evidence gaps and ensure HEOR priorities are incorporated into broader asset and franchise strategies.
  • Lead health economic research, including cost-effectiveness, budget impact, cost-of-illness, healthcare resource utilization, and other analyses that support understanding of the value of Travere therapies.
  • Develop and execute real-world evidence studies leveraging existing data sources, including administrative claims, electronic medical records, registries, and other healthcare databases, to characterize disease burden, treatment patterns, patient journeys, healthcare resource utilization, and clinical outcomes.
  • Lead the patient-reported outcomes strategy, including selection, development, validation, and incorporation of fit-for-purpose PRO measures into clinical development and evidence-generation programs where appropriate.
  • Partner with Clinical Development to incorporate HEOR and outcomes research considerations early in development, including study design, endpoint strategy, evidence gaps, and future access needs.
  • Identify opportunities to complement clinical trial evidence with epidemiology, real-world data, health economics, and patient-centered outcomes research.
  • Develop evidence that supports payer and health technology assessment needs and contributes to value dossiers, reimbursement submissions, and other access-related evidence requirements.
  • Anticipate future evidence needs and establish research plans that support new indications, lifecycle opportunities, and future nephrology assets.
  • Partner with external research collaborations, data partners, research organizations, and other external experts.
  • Develop and oversee HEOR publication plans and ensure timely dissemination of research through peer-reviewed publications, scientific congresses, and other appropriate scientific channels.
  • Represent Travere externally with HEOR researchers, nephrology experts, academic collaborators, and other scientific stakeholders.
  • Serve as an internal subject matter expert on health economics, outcomes research, real-world evidence, and patient-centered outcomes, providing strategic guidance to senior leadership and cross-functional teams.
  • Manage external vendors, research partners, budgets, timelines, and project execution to ensure high-quality and timely delivery of HEOR initiatives.
  • Ensure all activities are conducted in accordance with applicable laws, regulations, industry standards, company policies, and Travere compliance requirements.

Education/Experience Requirements:


  • Advanced degree in health economics, outcomes research, epidemiology, public health, health services research, pharmacy, medicine, biostatistics, or a related discipline required; PhD, PharmD, MD, ScD, DrPH, or equivalent advanced degree strongly preferred.
  • 12+ years of progressively responsible experience in HEOR, real-world evidence, outcomes research, market access evidence, or related disciplines within the biopharmaceutical industry, consulting, academia, or a combination thereof.
  • Demonstrated experience developing and executing HEOR and evidence-generation strategies for marketed and/or development-stage assets.
  • Strong experience using real-world healthcare data, including claims, EMR/EHR, registries, and other large healthcare databases.
  • Experience with health economic modeling, burden-of-illness research, healthcare resource utilization, epidemiology, and observational research.
  • Experience with patient-reported outcomes and clinical outcomes assessments, including instrument selection, development, validation, and implementation.
  • Experience developing evidence to support payer, reimbursement, and health technology assessment needs.
  • Experience in nephrology, rare disease, specialty therapeutics, or progressive chronic diseases strongly preferred.
  • Demonstrated record of scientific publications and presentations in HEOR, outcomes research, epidemiology, real-world evidence, or related fields.

Additional Skills/Experience/Requirements:


  • Strong understanding of payer and healthcare decision-maker evidence needs.
  • Ability to translate clinical and business questions into rigorous, decision-relevant evidence-generation programs.
  • Strong strategic thinking with the ability to anticipate evidence needs and connect research priorities to clinical development and product strategy.
  • Ability to work effectively across functions and influence senior leaders and cross-functional partners without direct authority.
  • Strong scientific judgment, analytical skills, and commitment to research quality and scientific integrity.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate complex evidence clearly to scientific and non-scientific audiences.
  • Strong leadership, organizational, budget management, and vendor management capabilities.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced and evolving organization.

Total Rewards Offerings:
Travere provides comprehensive total rewards offerings that demonstrate our commitment as a diverse, equitable, people-centric, and pay-for-performance organization.

Benefits: Our benefits include premium health, financial, work-life and well-being offerings for eligible employees and dependents, wellness and employee support programs, life insurance, disability, retirement plans with employer match and generous paid time off.

Compensation: Our competitive compensation package includes a combination of both cash compensation (base pay and short-term incentive) and long-term incentive compensation (company stock), designed to recognize, retain, and reward employees.

Target Base Pay Range:

$246,000.00 - $332,000.00

*This information is current as of the date of this posting and may be modified in the future. Actual pay offered to a candidate will depend on a variety of factors including the candidate’s experience, education, skills, and location.

Travere will accept applications on an ongoing basis until a candidate is selected for the position.

Travere Therapeutics, Inc. is an EEO/AA/Veteran/Disability Employer.

Job Description

About us

For over 100 years, Embry-Riddle has been the world's leading aviation and aerospace university, educating more than 30,000 students across residential campuses in Daytona Beach, Florida, and Prescott, Arizona, as well as through a global network of Worldwide locations and online programs. Working alongside industry leaders, government agencies and innovators, they are solving real-world challenges and shaping the technologies that will define tomorrow.

Whether you are an educator, researcher, administrator, technologist or industry professional, your work at Embry-Riddle will contribute to something bigger than a job. Join a community driven by discovery, purpose and excellence—and help shape the future of aerospace.


Job Description

Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University’s Worldwide campus is currently hiring adjunct faculty to teach SYSE 505 – System Safety and Certification

Course Description

Safety engineering considerations when designing, testing, and certifying airborne safety-critical systems in regulated industries. Fundamentals of system safety engineering and the regulatory framework for initial airworthiness certification; system hazard and risk analysis and safety assessment; safety requirements validation and verification; fault models and failure analysis techniques such as fault trees, FEMA, event tree analysis, common cause/mode analysis, dependence diagrams, and Markov analysis. Industry standards for aircraft development (SAE ARP4754B and ARP4761A) and for airborne hardware and software development (RTCA DO-178C and DO-254).


Please note that ERAU policy requires that all adjuncts be physically located within the United States while working for the University, including during training. Presently, we are able to support work for new adjuncts from all U.S. states except California. ERAU does not support work from international locations with some limited exceptions for individuals who are residing and working from U.S. military bases.

If selected for this role, the candidate will be required to provide proof of stated qualifications. This includes, but is not limited to, official transcripts, copies of professional licenses/certifications, documentation of military experience, and/or verified professional industry related experience.

Qualifications

Applicant Qualifications

18 graduate credit hours in any of the Teaching Disciplines within the doctoral program.


Applicable Experience

Experience at a Military and Civilian organization designing, developing, testing, operating, or analyzing application of unmanned systems (robotics), including the components, tools, methods, and processes associated with system control and interaction and Active membership in professional organizations in engineering, i.e., National Academy of Engineering, National Society of Professional Engineers, Society of Flight Test Engineers, Society of Experimental Test Pilots, Aircraft Designer, Human Factors and Ergonomics Society, or other field related to the research, design, development, test, evaluation, operation, or application of unmanned systems

jobs.excerpt: We are seeking a Senior QA Automation Engineer to join our Quality Engineering team and help ensure the reliability, security, and overall quality of our cybersecurity products.
jobs.description:
We are seeking a Senior QA Automation Engineer to join our Quality Engineering team and help ensure the reliability, security, and overall quality of our cybersecurity products. You will play a key role in defining, leading, and scaling quality assurance across our platform, with a strong emphasis on test automation.

This is a hands-on senior individual contributor role. You will lead our web application test automation efforts, designing and evolving automated testing solutions with Playwright and JavaScript, and integrating automated testing throughout the software development lifecycle. You will also mentor junior QA and automation engineers and influence engineering practices across teams.

Requirements

QA Strategy & Leadership

  • Lead the design and execution of QA strategies, frameworks, and automated test plans across multiple products
  • Identify high-value opportunities for automation and help define the team's automation strategy and roadmap
  • Participate in requirements and design reviews to identify quality risks and testability concerns early in the development lifecycle
  • Define meaningful quality metrics and provide visibility into automation coverage, reliability, and product quality
  • Continuously evaluate testing tools, techniques, and approaches, and drive improvement of QA processes aligned with engineering goals

Test Automation & Infrastructure

  • Lead the design, development, and ongoing improvement of our automated testing framework using Playwright and JavaScript
  • Develop reliable, maintainable, and reusable automated tests for browser-based cybersecurity applications, with coverage across backend, frontend, and infrastructure components
  • Establish and promote automation architecture, coding standards, design patterns, and testing best practices
  • Own and enhance CI/CD-integrated testing infrastructure, including quality gates and feedback mechanisms, for consistent validation across environments
  • Review existing automation and improve its reliability, maintainability, execution speed, and coverage
  • Diagnose and resolve flaky tests, automation failures, and complex application or environment issues
  • Analyze test results to distinguish product defects from automation, environment, and test-data issues
  • Contribute to our growing suite of automated security checks (e.g., SAST/DAST and dependency scanning) in CI/CD pipelines

Team Enablement & Collaboration

  • Mentor junior QA and automation engineers, conduct code reviews, and provide technical guidance
  • Partner with software engineers, product managers, security teams, and QA engineers to develop effective test strategies for new features and releases
  • Advocate for quality engineering practices and help shift testing earlier in the development lifecycle
  • Promote a culture of quality and accountability

What You Bring

Required:

  • 5+ years of experience in Software Quality Assurance, Quality Engineering, Software Development Engineering in Test (SDET), or a similar role
  • Strong experience designing and developing automated tests for modern web applications
  • Hands-on experience with Playwright, preferably using JavaScript or TypeScript, with emphasis on designing scalable automation frameworks rather than solely creating individual test cases (experience with Cypress, Selenium, Jest, or similar is a plus)
  • Strong understanding of software testing methodologies, including functional, integration, regression, end-to-end, and negative testing
  • Strong experience integrating automated tests with CI/CD pipelines (e.g., GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, CircleCI) and source-control workflows
  • Experience testing complex applications involving role-based access controls, permissions, multi-tenant environments, or security policies
  • Experience mentoring junior engineers and providing constructive technical feedback through code reviews
  • Strong communication skills and ability to work cross-functionally

Preferred:

  • Familiarity with Docker, Kubernetes, AWS, Azure, or similar technologies
  • Experience in security-critical, high-availability, or infrastructure-heavy systems
  • Familiarity with API security, authentication flows, and data protection practices
  • Experience leading QA initiatives in Agile environments
  • Familiarity with security testing tools (e.g., OWASP ZAP, Burp Suite, SAST/DAST)

What Success Looks Like:

Success means moving beyond simply increasing the number of automated tests. You will build an automation ecosystem that engineers trust: tests that are reliable, maintainable, appropriately scoped, and give rapid feedback when something goes wrong. You will become a technical leader within the QA organization, helping decide what to automate, how to automate it, and how automation fits into the broader development process, while growing the engineers around you.

You as a Person

  • Knowledge: Deep expertise in QA automation and CI/CD workflows
  • Skill: Builds scalable testing systems and mentors others in quality practices
  • Ability: Influences teams and drives improvements in product quality

You in the Role

  • Autonomy: Owns and evolves QA and test automation across multiple products
  • Complexity: Solves complex quality challenges across the full stack
  • Impact: Ensures consistent, high-quality product releases

Extra Credit

  • QA certifications such as ISTQB, or security certifications such as OSCP, CEH, or CSSLP
  • Experience with SaaS platforms or networking-intensive solutions
  • Hands-on experience with cloud security and compliance (FedRAMP, SOC 2, ISO 27001)

Benefits

Why Dispel/Benefits

At Dispel you’ll be rewarded and recognized for your performance in an environment that will challenge you and give you clear direction on what it takes to succeed in your role as well as provide development for other roles you may be interested in.

  • Base salary: $90,000 – $120,000
  • 401(k) with company match
  • Generous paid time off and holidays
  • Performance bonus and equity eligible
  • Remote work
  • Medical, vision, dental insurance

Position Title: Intern

Location: Remote, but must be a college student/recent graduate residing in the U.S.

About the Active Minds Internship Program

Active Minds is the nation’s leading nonprofit organization changing the culture around mental health. Through our presence at more than 800 high school and college campuses, in corporate settings, and with a wide-reaching public audience, Active Minds is creating communities of support and saving lives. Founded in 2003 by Alison Malmon after the tragic suicide of her brother Brian, Active Minds is dedicated to supporting a new generation in ending the silence, helping to make mental health as highly valued as physical health. Through our many programs – including the emotionally gripping Send Silence Packing® traveling exhibit and our compelling Active Minds Speakers – we are changing culture and behaviors related to mental health across the country.

Our internships are geared towards current college students and recent college graduates. As a small nonprofit, Active Minds relies on the help of our interns tremendously. They work directly on important initiatives and projects and assist staff on a variety of administrative tasks. Interns have the opportunity to do substantive work, gain experience in the nonprofit sector, and help change the culture around mental health.

All Spring 2027 internships will be remote, with an anticipated start date of February 1st, 2027, and an anticipated end date of April 23rd, 2027. We expect interns to work a minimum of 20 hours a week, set a consistent work schedule between 9:00am and 5:00pm EST Monday through Friday, and commit to staying on board for the entire semester (February-April).

Active Minds pays interns $18 per hour.

This role will provide interns with the opportunity to be creative, learn how nonprofits manage and develop their social media, collaborate with various Active Minds staffers to learn more about mental health advocacy, and interact with thousands of enthusiastic audience members on a daily basis.

We are looking for a Lead Data Scientist – Virtual Models to take ownership of this programme from the start.

This is a hands-on role for an experienced data scientist who wants to build something new. You will assess existing datasets across QIMA’s Business Units, identify the most promising opportunities, develop proof-of-concept models and prepare them for use by internal teams and, ultimately, by clients.

Initial applications may include models related to:

  • skin;
  • hair follicles;
  • longevity;
  • prostate cancer;
  • immunology.

You will work closely with Managing Directors, laboratory scientists and QIMA’s IT and AI experts. Scientific validation will be carried out in collaboration with independent laboratory teams.

Key responsibilities

  • Review and assess proposals from QIMA’s Business Units.
  • Examine the underlying data in detail, including its quality, structure, consistency, depth and breadth.
  • Recommend one or two models with the strongest potential for development, subject to approval by the CEO of QIMA Life Sciences.
  • Build and manage the required data pipelines.
  • Clean, structure, integrate and analyse complex biological datasets.
  • Develop machine learning models and proof of concepts.
  • Identify data gaps and recommend additional experiments where needed. Work with laboratory scientists to help define these experiments, including the required data, measurements and quality criteria.
  • Establish clear validation criteria and prepare models for independent scientific validation.
  • Improve the models through repeated testing and iteration.
  • Ensure that code, data and models are reproducible, traceable and properly documented.
  • Present results clearly to scientific, technical, commercial and non-specialist audiences.
  • Support the preparation of a model for future commercialisation, either as a SaaS product or as a service supporting, replacing or complementing wet-lab assays.
  • Contribute to the documentation and protection of intellectual property related to the models, pipelines and methods.

This role will initially be an individual contributor position. As the programme grows, you may help build and lead a team of additional data scientists.

First objectives

Within the first six months, you will be expected to:

  • assess the main model proposals and their underlying datasets;
  • recommend the one or two strongest projects;
  • establish a proof of concept for one or two models.

Within 12 to 15 months, the objective will be to prepare at least one model for potential commercialisation. This should include sufficient scientific validation, an interface usable internally, and complete documentation or detailed operator training.

You have:

  • a PhD in data science, biostatistics, bioinformatics, machine learning or a related field;
  • 8–10 years of experience in data science, biostatistics and machine learning;
  • a proven track record of delivering complex machine learning projects using complex biological datasets;
  • strong experience building data pipelines, assessing data quality, identifying limitations and defining what additional data is needed;
  • experience working with scientists and translating scientific questions into data and modelling approaches;
  • excellent communication skills and the ability to explain complex concepts clearly to non-specialists;
  • ideally, experience presenting work to clients, partners or other external stakeholders;
  • a practical, entrepreneurial and hands-on approach;
  • the ability to work independently and take ownership of an ambiguous, new project.

Experience in a specific therapeutic area is not essential. The most important requirements are strong technical expertise, experience with biological data and the ability to turn complex datasets into useful, validated models.

Strong Python or R skills, including production-quality, version-controlled code. Experience with cloud data platforms (we use Snowflake) and MLOps practices.

Why join QIMA?

This is an opportunity to build a new capability from the ground up and shape how QIMA uses its biological data. You will have direct access to senior leadership, laboratory experts and technical teams, with the autonomy to define the approach and deliver tangible results.

The role will be based in Europe and will require travel, depending on project needs, to QIMA laboratories in France, Northern Ireland and Germany.

Does this describe you? Then we want to hear from you as soon as possible! Apply now with your CV in Englishand we can write the next chapter of the QIMA story together!

At QIMA, we are on a mission to help our clients make products consumers can trust. We have developed compliance solutions for testing, inspection and certification (TIC) that enable supply chain agility, sustainability and product innovation. Our services are used by 30,000 businesses globally in the consumer products, agri-food and life sciences industries. Backed by 6,000+ dedicated Qimates worldwide, we bring local expertise and tailored support to every client. Our passion for service has made QIMA an industry leader for customer satisfaction, as highlighted by our exceptional Net Promoter Score (NPS).

Through our Life Sciences activities, we develop and deliver scientific testing and research services for our clients.

We are now launching a new programme to develop virtual pharmacology models. These models will use the data generated through years of laboratory work to help assess the efficacy of molecules and support future screening activities.

The University of Miami Information Technology & Systems Department has an exciting opportunity for a full-time Enterprise Integration Solutions Architect.


The Enterprise Integration Solutions Architect provides advanced technical expertise in the design, governance, and implementation of enterprise integration and interoperability solutions. The position is responsible for evaluating complex business and technical requirements, developing cross-platform integration strategies, establishing architectural standards and designing innovative solutions that enable secure and efficient exchange of information across enterprise applications, cloud technologies, APIs, and emerging digital platforms.


The role serves as a senior technical resource for complex initiatives involving interoperability, integration architecture, and emerging technologies while supporting the organization's long-term technology strategy.

Core Responsibilities:


  • Develops and maintains enterprise integration architectures, standards, and design patterns to support interoperability across applications, platforms, and technologies.
  • Evaluates complex business, operational, and technical requirements and translates them into scalable integration and interoperability solutions.
  • Designs, architects, and implements solutions utilizing APIs, cloud services, middleware, and other integration technologies.
  • Establishes governance practices, technical standards, and best practices related to enterprise integration and interoperability.
  • Leads the evaluation of emerging technologies and recommends innovative solutions that enhance operational effectiveness and organizational capabilities.
  • Collaborates with technical and business stakeholders to define integration strategies supporting enterprise objectives.
  • Provides technical consultation and architectural guidance for complex initiatives involving multiple systems, vendors, and technologies.
  • Develops prototypes, proof-of-concepts, and solution designs to address unique business and technical challenges.
  • Supports the resolution of complex integration and interoperability issues and provides guidance on architectural decisions.
  • Facilitates technical reviews to ensure alignment with enterprise architecture standards, security requirements, and technology strategies.
  • Maintains knowledge of industry trends, standards, and evolving technologies related to interoperability, integration architecture, cloud platforms, and digital innovation.
  • Partners with vendors and third-party providers to evaluate solutions, establish technical requirements, and support implementation efforts.
  • Develops and maintains technical documentation, architecture diagrams, standards, and governance artifacts.
  • Mentors technical team members and promotes best practices related to enterprise integration and solution architecture.
  • Adheres to University and unit-level policies and procedures and safeguards University assets.

Department Specific Functions:

Epic Technical Architecture

  • Serve as the technical lead for Epic interoperability and integration solutions involving Epic and third-party applications.
  • Design, implement, and support solutions utilizing Epic Chronicles, Bridges, Interconnect, Care Everywhere, Clarity, Epic FHIR services, APIs, Cache Object Script, and SMART on FHIR.
  • Evaluate and recommend appropriate Epic integration approaches based on business and technical requirements.
  • Develop or guide custom integrations, web services, and interoperability solutions using Epic-supported technologies.
  • Lead technical planning for Epic upgrades, interface migrations, vendor implementations, and platform modernization initiatives.
  • Epic application certification in a clinical or revenue cycle module, or equivalent experience supporting Epic clinical and revenue cycle workflows, is a plus.
  • Collaborate with Epic application teams, integration engineers, security teams, and vendors to deliver end-to-end solutions.

Healthcare Interoperability and Solution Architecture

  • Design enterprise interoperability solutions connecting Epic with clinical, operational, research, and digital health platforms.
  • Apply healthcare interoperability standards including FHIR, HL7 v2/v3, C-CDA, DICOM, APIs, and related integration patterns.
  • Lead the architecture, implementation, administration, and support of interoperability solutions utilizing healthcare integration platforms such as InterSystems IRIS for Health, Rhapsody, Corepoint, and other enterprise integration technologies.
  • Translate business and clinical requirements into secure, scalable, and supportable architectures.
  • Establish reusable integration patterns, technical standards, and architecture guidelines.
  • Ensure solutions align with enterprise architecture, cybersecurity, data governance, and operational requirements.

Vendor and Startup Engagement

  • Lead technical discussions, architecture reviews, and solution assessments with healthcare vendors, startups, and implementation partners.
  • Evaluate vendor products for interoperability, scalability, security, operational supportability, and alignment with organizational standards.
  • Provide technical due diligence, architecture guidance, and build-versus-buy recommendations.
  • Review vendor APIs, implementation guides, security models, and integration designs.
  • Facilitate architecture workshops and drive practical solutions for complex business and technical challenges.

Software Engineering and Technical Prototyping

  • Develop or guide prototypes, proofs of concept, web services, APIs, and custom integration components.
  • Apply software engineering best practices for API design, security, testing, logging, exception handling, and source control.
  • Mentor engineers and participate in the design and development of complex interoperability solutions.
  • Develop and review complex SQL for data extraction, transformation, reconciliation, reporting, and troubleshooting.
  • Incorporate security, privacy, and compliance requirements into all solution designs.
  • Partner with cybersecurity and infrastructure teams to ensure HIPAA-compliant and secure interoperability solutions.
  • Participate in security reviews, risk assessments, and vendor evaluations.

AI-Enabled and Agentic Solutions

  • Evaluate emerging AI, automation, and agentic technologies to improve interoperability, operations, and healthcare workflows.
  • Design and prototype AI-enabled solutions integrating enterprise systems, APIs, workflows, and healthcare data.
  • Assess AI platform capabilities, security, governance, and operational considerations.
  • Collaborate with business, clinical, security, and compliance stakeholders to ensure responsible AI adoption.

Operational Reliability and Production Support

  • Provide ongoing operational support for Epic interoperability technologies, including Epic Bridges interfaces, APIs, and Integration Engine platforms.
  • Serve as a senior escalation point for complex production issues involving integrations, applications, databases, networks, and vendors.
  • Lead troubleshooting, root cause analysis, and remediation efforts for critical interoperability workflows.
  • Ensure solutions are designed with appropriate monitoring, alerting, resiliency, disaster recovery, and operational support processes.
  • Drive continuous improvement of reliability, performance, supportability, and operational excellence across the integration ecosystem.

This list of duties and responsibilities is not intended to be all-inclusive and may be expanded to include other duties or responsibilities as necessary.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:


  • Bachelor’s degree in computer science, Software Engineering, Information Systems, Information Technology, Healthcare Informatics, or a related field. Master’s degree in computer science, Information Systems, or a related discipline preferred.
  • Minimum 8 years of experience in healthcare IT, software engineering, systems integration, interoperability, application development, or technology architecture.
  • One or more Epic technical certifications preferred (Epic Chronicles, Epic Bridges, Epic Interconnect, Epic Clarity, or Epic Care Everywhere certification)
  • InterSystems IRIS for Health or HealthShare Health Connect certification or comparable healthcare integration engine certification is a plus
  • HL7 or FHIR-related certification is a plus
  • Demonstrated experience integrating third-party applications with Epic in a healthcare provider environment.
  • Strong working knowledge of healthcare interoperability standards, including: FHIR , HL7 v2 , HL7 v3, C-CDA ,DICOM, SMART on FHIR
  • Strong understanding of REST APIs, SOAP services, JSON, XML, API contracts, webhooks, and enterprise integration patterns.
  • Experience with key components of the Epic technical ecosystem, such as Chronicles, Bridges, Interconnect, Care Everywhere, Clarity, or Epic FHIR services.
  • Hands-on programming experience using Caché/ InterSystems ObjectScript, Python, or a comparable programming language.
  • Experience designing or developing custom web services, APIs, or enterprise integration components.
  • Advanced knowledge of relational databases and strong SQL skills.
  • Experience with PL/SQL, Transact-SQL, stored procedures, database functions, performance optimization, or comparable database programming.
  • Experience engaging directly with vendors and evaluating vendor-proposed technical solutions.
  • Experience facilitating technical discovery, architecture workshops, design reviews, and solution assessments.
  • Experience designing solutions that handle confidential clinical, patient, or other regulated healthcare information.
  • Ability to produce clear architecture diagrams, technical specifications, decision records, and implementation guidance.
  • Experience presenting complex technical concepts to both technical and nontechnical audiences.
  • Demonstrated ability to work independently and lead work across multiple technical and business teams.
  • Strong analytical, troubleshooting, communication, facilitation, and problem-solving skills.
  • Learning Agility: Ability to learn new procedures, technologies, and protocols, and adapt to changing priorities and work demands.
  • Teamwork: Ability to work collaboratively with others and contribute to a team environment.
  • Technical Proficiency: Skilled in using office software, technology, and relevant computer applications.

jobs.excerpt: OverviewDecisionPoint seeks a Journeyman Vulnerability Management / ACAS Analyst to support vulnerability tracking, remediation coordination, and cybersecurity compliance reporting for the USMEPCOM ENLIST program.
jobs.description:
Overview

DecisionPoint seeks a Journeyman Vulnerability Management / ACAS Analyst to support vulnerability tracking, remediation coordination, and cybersecurity compliance reporting for the USMEPCOM ENLIST program.

The Vulnerability Management / ACAS Analyst will review ACAS findings provided by Government personnel, reconcile affected systems and devices with inventory records, and coordinate corrective actions with responsible administrators. The analyst will track remediation tickets, dependencies, deadlines, POA&M updates, and supporting evidence through resolution.

This role will also coordinate Government rescans, review the resulting data to verify remediation, and maintain accurate vulnerability status information for operational reporting, compliance reviews, and cybersecurity inspections.

This position is remote, with a preference for candidates located in the Chicago area.

Note: By applying to this position, you acknowledge and consent to having your resume included in an active competitive government contract bid.

Duties & Responsibilities

The Vulnerability Management / ACAS Analyst will:

  • Review ACAS vulnerability findings provided by Government personnel.
  • Analyze findings to identify affected assets, systems, applications, devices, and responsible support teams.
  • Reconcile affected assets against configuration-management, inventory, and asset-management records.
  • Research discrepancies between ACAS results and authoritative asset inventories.
  • Support prioritization of vulnerabilities based on severity, asset criticality, mission impact, remediation deadlines, and Government direction.
  • Coordinate corrective actions with system administrators, infrastructure teams, application teams, engineers, and other remediation owners.
  • Create, update, and monitor vulnerability-remediation tickets in the designated workflow system.
  • Track assigned owners, corrective actions, technical dependencies, target completion dates, and current remediation status.
  • Follow up with responsible personnel to obtain status updates and identify issues that could delay remediation.
  • Collect technical documentation, screenshots, configuration results, ticket records, and other evidence supporting remediation completion.
  • Review supporting evidence for completeness before requesting validation or rescanning.
  • Coordinate Government rescan requests for vulnerabilities reported as remediated.
  • Review Government-provided rescan results to verify that corrective actions successfully resolved identified vulnerabilities.
  • Document validated closures and retain supporting evidence in the designated Government repository.
  • Track compliance with applicable Information Assurance Vulnerability Alerts and Information Assurance Vulnerability Management requirements.
  • Create and update POA&M entries for vulnerabilities requiring formal corrective-action tracking.
  • Maintain accurate vulnerability status information for recurring reports, dashboards, compliance reviews, and cybersecurity inspections.
  • Identify overdue, high-risk, recurring, or unresolved findings and escalate them to the Senior Vulnerability Management / ACAS Response Analyst or cybersecurity leadership.
  • Track remediation dependencies involving patch availability, configuration changes, application testing, maintenance windows, or operational constraints.
  • Assist with documenting false positives, mitigating controls, operational dependencies, and Government-approved risk decisions.
  • Support review of Endpoint Security Solutions reports and tracking of applicable endpoint-security findings.
  • Develop vulnerability aging reports, remediation status summaries, compliance metrics, and supporting briefing materials.
  • Help identify recurring vulnerabilities, process gaps, inaccurate asset records, and opportunities to improve remediation workflows.
  • Support maintenance of vulnerability-management procedures, standard operating procedures, tracking tools, and reporting templates.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

  • Active Secret clearance or higher.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Cybersecurity, Information Systems, or a related field.
  • Minimum of 7 years of relevant cybersecurity, information assurance, vulnerability-management, or information-security experience.
  • Current CompTIA Security+ certification.

Preferred Qualifications

  • CompTIA Cybersecurity Analyst (CySA+) certification.
  • Experience reviewing ACAS or Tenable vulnerability-scan results in a Department of Defense environment.
  • Experience reconciling vulnerability findings against hardware, software, configuration-management, or asset-inventory records.
  • Experience coordinating vulnerability remediation with system administrators, infrastructure teams, and application support teams.
  • Knowledge of Information Assurance Vulnerability Alerts and Information Assurance Vulnerability Management requirements.
  • Experience creating and maintaining cybersecurity POA&Ms.
  • Experience using ServiceNow or another ticketing and workflow-management platform to track remediation activities.
  • Familiarity with Endpoint Security Solutions, STIG Viewer, SCAP tools, eMASS, or comparable DoD cybersecurity technologies.
  • Knowledge of the DoD Risk Management Framework, NIST SP 800-53 controls, DISA Security Technical Implementation Guides, and applicable DoD cybersecurity directives.
  • Experience collecting, reviewing, and maintaining technical evidence supporting vulnerability remediation and closure.
  • Experience coordinating rescans and reviewing results to verify successful remediation.
  • Experience preparing vulnerability reports, remediation metrics, aging summaries, dashboards, or inspection-support materials.
  • Familiarity with current DoD 8140 cybersecurity workforce qualification requirements.
  • Strong analytical, organizational, documentation, communication, and follow-through skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple findings, owners, dependencies, and deadlines in a structured compliance environment.

Senior Consultant – Product Security & Compliance (Connected Products) 

Location: United States (Remote) 

Business Unit: Cyber Security  

 

Imagine your customer is a leading industrial component manufacturer, specializing in top-notch manufacturing and transportation equipment. You have ambitious goals: to streamline processes, ensure top-quality security for your client’s products, and assure cybersecurity. That’s where you come in.  Our analysis will bridge any gaps across design, engineering, SDLC and technical control testing, and regulatory readiness, helping clients meet requirements such as the EU CRA, IEC 62443, and other product security standards.

With our expertise in testing, inspection and independent security validation services, you will assist your client in raising their cyber resilience like never before. Your success story? It's written in client readiness and satisfaction, secure products, and audit-defensible evidence. Now also imagine the same story, but for products such as vehicles, medical devices, ships, IoT products, network equipment, software products, etc. Doesn’t it sound like an exciting mission?  

 

Bureau Veritas Cybersecurity provides cybersecurity services covering people, organization,  technology, of products, and connected ecosystems. 

 

We have reputable clients and they request expertise to increase their level of cybersecurity, and regulatory readiness.

Role Overview 

The Senior Consultant – Product Security & Compliance is a doer role responsible for delivering product security and compliance engagements while supporting the growth of Bureau Veritas’ Cyber Security services across North America. 

This role focuses on helping clients translate regulatory requirements for North American customers, into practical, engineering-aligned product security controls, harmonized with frameworks across sectors with current compliance standards and frameworks 

The individual will work across industrial, IoT, embedded, software, medical technology, transportation, and cloud-connected product environments, supporting execution of engagements, development of repeatable offerings, and business development activities. 

Key Responsibilities

 

1. Client Engagement Delivery 

  • Execute and support delivery of product security consulting engagements, including: 
    • Product security maturity assessments 
    • CRA, IEC 62443, IoT security, automotive, medical device,- standards and regulatory readiness and gap assessments 
    • Threat modeling, abuse case analysis, and product risk assessments 
    • Secure architecture review and security requirement definition for connected products 
    • Secure product development lifecycle (PDL/SDL) and technical product technical requirements implementation support 
    • Product security, maturity modelling, scoring, heatmaps, and remediation roadmaps 
  • Translate regulatory and standard requirements into engineering actions, test cases, control frameworks, and evidence expectations 
  • Produce structured, audit-defensible deliverables aligned to BV methodologies 

2. Regulatory Harmonization & Product Security Compliance 

  • Apply and operationalize product cybersecurity regulatory frameworks across engagements 
  • Support harmonization and implementation across product security regulations and standards, including: 
  • Regulatory Standards and Frameworks: 
    • EU Cyber Resilience Act (CRA)  
    • NIS2 Directive 
    • Relevant North American IoT security initiatives (e.g., NIST, FCC, and related connected-device security expectations) 
  • Secure Development Lifecycle & Process Standards: 
    • IEC 62443-4-1 
    • NIST Secure Software Development Framework (SSDF)
    • OWASP SAMM 
    • ISO/IEC 27034  and secure software engineering practices 
  • Technical Security Requirements & Baselines: 
    • EU Common Criteria 
    • IEC 62443-4-2 
    • ETSI EN 303 645 (IoT security) 
    • NIST IoT cybersecurity guidance 
    • OWASP ASVS and API security frameworks 
  • Software Supply Chain & SBOM: 
    • SBOM standards and formats (SPDX, Cyclone-DX) 
    • NIST supply chain risk management guidance 
  • Sector-Specific Frameworks (as applicable): 
    • ISO/SAE 21434 and UNECE R155/R156 (automotive) 
    • FDA and MDCG cybersecurity guidance (medical devices) 
    • ISO 14971 (medical risk management) 
  • Develop and use: 
    • Control mappings, and CRA/IEC/sector-specific requirement crosswalks 
    • Evidence matrices, assessment checklists, and regulatory traceability models 
    • Compliance scoring models, maturity models, heatmaps, and remediation roadmaps 
    • Help clients move from regulatory interpretation → implementation → verification → readiness 

3. Product Security Engineering & Architecture Support 

  • Support clients in securing connected product architectures, including: 
    • Embedded systems and firmware, device operating systems, and product interfaces 
    • Industrial and IoT devices, network equipment, and operational technology components 
    • Software applications, APIs, and web management interfaces 
    • Cloud-connected product backends, and supporting infrastructure 
  • Contribute to: 
    • Threat models 
    • Security architecture definitions 
    • Identity, communication, and data protection strategies 
  • Assist in defining aligned technical product security requirements and validation criteria mapped to EU CC, CRA, IEC 62443, OWASP, NIST, ETSI, and sector-specific expectations 

4. Security Verification & Validation Support 

  • Contribute to product and system-level security validation activities, 
  • Support development of test cases, validation frameworks and evidence packages aligned to regulatory and standard requirements 
  • Help structure outputs into certification and regulations ready evidence packages 

5. Business Development (Seller-Doer Expectation) 

  • Support growth of product security, and regulatory compliance  services through: 
    • Client discussions, technical solutioning and discovery workshops 
    • Proposal development and response support 
    • Participation in discovery workshops and scoping sessions 
  • Help position BV as a trusted partner for product security, CRA readiness, and connected-product assurance 
  • Contribute to service offering development and reusable artifacts 

6. Capability Development & Team Contribution 

  • Contribute to building repeatable product security, and compliance methodologies and templates 
  • Support development of: 
    • Regulatory aligned frameworks 
    • Product security assessment models 
    • Testing and validation structures 
  • Mentor junior consultants and support team knowledge development 
  • Collaborate with global BV teams and technical specialists 

Required Experience 

Core Experience 

  • 6–10 years of experience in cybersecurity with exposure to product security, industrial systems, embedded systems, or connected devices 
  • Experience working in consulting or client-facing delivery roles 
  • Hands-on involvement in security assessments, risk analysis, vulnerability management, or architecture engagements 

Technical Competencies

  • Understanding of: 
    • Threat modeling and risk assessment methodologies 
    • Secure development lifecycle (SDL) concepts 
    • Product and system security architecture 
    • Software supply chain security (SBOM, SCA) 
  • Knowledge of various laws and regulations related to cyber product security, as well as the current developments in this area.  
  • Exposure to security testing techniques across device, firmware, application, hardware, or system layers is a strong plus 

Consulting & Personal Attributes 

  • Strong structured problem-solving, evidence review, and documentation skills 
  • Ability to balance technical depth with client communication, and engineering practicality 
  • Results-oriented with a seller-doer mindset, and ability to support business development 
  • Comfortable working across multiple industries, product types, and stakeholder groups 
  • Willingness to travel for onsite engagements as needed 

Preferred Experience 

  • Experience delivering IEC 62443, IoT security, automotive cybersecurity, medical-device cybersecurity,
  • Experience in technical operations of areas such as SBOM, PSIRT, standards and regulatory readiness, 
  • Experience creating control mappings, evidence matrices, requirement crosswalks, assessment checklists, report templates, or regulatory-readiness frameworks 
  • Relevant certifications such as CISSP, CSSLP, GICSP, ISA/IEC 62443 certificates, ISO 27001 Lead Implementer/Auditor, or equivalent practical experience are helpful but not mandatory 

WHAT CAN YOU EXPECT FROM US?  

We are an organization with a strong focus on technical cybersecurity, delivering high-quality technical services in the field of digital security. You will be part of a team of motivated international specialists, where knowledge exchange is highly valued.  

At Bureau Veritas Cybersecurity, we provide an environment for you to develop your talents and stimulate your professional growth. Together, we work to safeguard the security and integrity of valuable data while facing the challenges of the ever-evolving digital world. Bureau Veritas Cybersecurity is a fast-growing company with ambitious goals. You will have the opportunity to grow along with us and shape your career allowing you to become an expert in your field.  

In terms of content, we offer you a diverse portfolio of exciting clients and projects. We are part of Bureau Veritas, which means that international opportunities are expanding, both for project work and for advancing your career.

The Chief Crypto Officer (CCO) is responsible for leading the organization's cryptocurrency, blockchain, digital asset, and Web3 strategy. This executive develops and oversees crypto-related products, services, partnerships, regulatory compliance, risk management, and innovation initiatives. The role ensures that the organization remains competitive within the rapidly evolving digital asset ecosystem while maintaining security, governance, and regulatory standards.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership

  • Develop and execute the organization's cryptocurrency and digital asset strategy.
  • Identify emerging opportunities in blockchain, decentralized finance (DeFi), tokenization, stablecoins, and digital asset custody.
  • Advise executive leadership and the Board on crypto market developments and trends.
  • Drive innovation through blockchain-based business models and digital asset solutions.
  • Establish long-term growth plans for crypto-related business lines.

Digital Asset Management

  • Oversee cryptocurrency treasury management and digital asset portfolios.
  • Develop policies governing the acquisition, custody, transfer, and storage of digital assets.
  • Monitor market conditions and recommend asset allocation strategies.
  • Ensure robust wallet management and digital asset security protocols.

Product & Business Development

  • Lead development of crypto-enabled products and services.
  • Identify strategic partnerships with exchanges, custodians, blockchain networks, and fintech providers.
  • Evaluate opportunities for tokenization, smart contracts, NFTs, and decentralized applications (dApps).
  • Support go-to-market strategies for blockchain and digital asset initiatives.

Regulatory Compliance & Governance

  • Monitor global regulatory developments impacting digital assets.
  • Work closely with Legal, Compliance, Risk, and Audit teams.
  • Establish governance frameworks for blockchain and crypto operations.

Risk Management

  • Assess operational, market, liquidity, custody, and counterparty risks.

Stakeholder Engagement

  • Represent the organization in industry forums, regulatory discussions, and blockchain communities.
  • Build relationships with regulators, technology providers, investors, and industry associations.

Team Leadership

  • DeFi, stablecoins, CBDCs, and emerging digital asset technologies.

  • Financial Acumen
  • Technology Leadership
  • Stakeholder Management
  • Change Management
  • Executive Communication
  • Decision Making

FULL-TIME REMOTE CUSTOMER SERVICE REPRESENTATIVE (NOVA SCOTIA)

We offer many advancement opportunities, including Supervisor, Trainer, Talent Acquisition, and Operations Management.

POSITION RESPONSIBILITIES

WHAT DOES A WORK AT HOME CONTACT CENTER REPRESENTATIVE DO?

This position supports customer service, technical support, and customer sales interactions. This role requires you to interact with hundreds of customers each week across the country to resolve support issues, sell new products and services, and ensure best in class customer experience. In addition to being the best in the business when it comes to customer interactions, you will need to be confident, fully engaged, a team player, and dedicated to bringing a positive and enthusiastic outlook to work each day.

  • Listen to customers, understand their needs, and resolve customer issues

  • Recognize sales opportunity and apply sales skills to upgrade
  • Explain and position the products and processes with customers
  • Appropriately escalate customer dissatisfaction with managerial team

CANDIDATE QUALIFICATIONS

WONDER IF YOU ARE A GOOD FIT?

MCI provides all new employees with world-class training, so all positive, driven, and confident applicants are encouraged to apply. Ideal candidates for this position are highly motivated, energetic, and dedicated.

Qualifications

  • Must be 18 years of age or older
  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Excellent organizational, written, and oral communication skills
  • The ability to type swiftly and accurately (20+ words a minute)
  • Basic knowledge of Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, PowerPoint, Word, Outlook)
  • Basic understanding of Windows operating system
  • Highly reliable with the ability to maintain regular attendance and punctuality

  • Ability to multi-task, stay focused and self-manage
  • Strong team orientation and customer focus
  • The ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment where change and ambiguity prevalent
  • Excellent interpersonal skills and the ability to build relationships with your team and customers

COMPENSATION DETAILS

WANT AN EMPLOYER THAT VALUES YOUR CONTRIBUTION?

At MCI, we believe that your hard work deserves recognition and reward. Our compensation and benefits packages are designed to be competitive and to grow with you over time. Starting compensation is based on experience, and we offer a variety of benefits and incentives to support and reward our team members.

What You Can Expect from MCI:

We understand the importance of balance and support, which is why we offer a variety of benefits and incentives that go beyond a paycheck. Our team members enjoy:

  • Paid Time Off: Earn PTO and paid holidays to take the time you need.
  • Health Benefits: Full-time employees are eligible for supplemental health coverage through Blue Cross.
  • Life Insurance: Access life insurance options to safeguard your loved ones.
  • Supplemental Insurance: Accident and critical illness insurance
  • Career Growth: With a focus on internal promotions, employees enjoy significant advancement opportunities.
  • Paid Training: Learn new skills while earning a paycheck.
  • Fun, Engaging Work Environment: Enjoy a team-oriented culture that fosters collaboration and engagement.
  • Casual Dress Code: Be comfortable while you work.

Compensation & Benefits that Fit Your Life

MCI takes pride in tailoring our offerings to fit the needs of our diverse team across subsidiaries and locations. While specific benefits and incentives may vary by geography, the core of our commitment remains the same: rewarding effort, providing growth opportunities, and creating an environment where every employee feels valued.

If you’re ready to join a company that recognizes your contributions and supports your growth, MCI is the place for you. Apply today!

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

This job operates in a professional office environment. While performing the duties of this job, the employee will be largely sedentary and will be required to sit/stand for long periods while using a computer and telephone headset. The employee will be regularly required to operate a computer and other office equipment, including a phone, copier, and printer. The employee may occasionally be required to move about the office to accomplish tasks; reach in any direction; raise or lower objects, move objects from place to place, hold onto objects, and move or exert force up to forty (40) pounds.

All MCI Locations

Subject to the program and location of the position

The policy regarding requests for reasonable accommodation applies to all aspects of employment. If reasonable accommodations are needed, please contact Human Resources.

At MCI and its subsidiaries, we embrace differences and believe diversity is a benefit to our employees, our company, our customers, and our community. All aspects of employment at MCI are based solely on a person's merit and qualifications. ABOUT US

MCI helps customers take on their CX and DX challenges differently, creating industry-leading solutions that deliver exceptional experiences and drive optimal performance. MCI assists companies with business process outsourcing, staff augmentation, contact center customer services, and IT Services needs by providing general and specialized hosting, software, staff, and services.

In 2019, Marlowe Companies Inc. (MCI) was named by Inc. Magazine as Iowa’s Fastest Growing Company in the State of Iowa and was named the 452nd Fastest Growing Privately Company in the USA, making the coveted top 500 for the first time. MCI now employs 10,000+ talented individuals with 150+ diverse North American client partners across the following MCI brands: MCI BPO, MCI BPOaaS, MarketForce, GravisApps, Gravis Marketing, MarchEast, Mass Markets, MCI Federal Services (MFS), OnBrand24, The Sydney Call Center, Valor Intelligent Processing (VIP), BYC Aqua, EastWest BPO, TeleTechnology, and Vinculum.

We are the leading provider of professional services to the middle market globally, our purpose is to instill confidence in a world of change, empowering our clients and people to realize their full potential. Our exceptional people are the key to our unrivaled, culture and talent experience and our ability to be compelling to our clients. You’ll find an environment that inspires and empowers you to thrive both personally and professionally. There’s no one like you and that’s why there’s nowhere like RSM.

The Learning & Development Business Partner Director serves as a senior strategic learning and capability advisor to an assigned line of business and its leaders. This role translates business, workforce, and talent priorities into an integrated capability strategy that strengthens performance, builds professional readiness, and advances RSM’s First Choice Advisor strategy.


As a member of the L&D leadership team, the Director helps shape the future of learning at RSM, including operating models, workforce capability strategies, service delivery, and technology adoption. The Director builds trusted relationships across the business, L&D, and Talent to mobilize expertise, scale effective solutions, and lead complex initiatives with meaningful business impact.


Key Responsibilities

Business and Capability Strategy

  • Build trusted relationships with senior business and talent leaders, serving as a first-choice advisor on workforce capability, performance, and development priorities.
  • Translate firm, talent, and business strategies into multi-year capability roadmaps with clear priorities, outcomes, measures, and investment needs.
  • Apply performance consulting and systems thinking to distinguish capability needs from process, role clarity, technology, capacity, leadership, and other performance barriers.
  • Anticipate emerging capability risks and opportunities and advise leaders on priorities and the right mix of learning, experience, coaching, performance support, knowledge resources, and technology-enabled solutions.

Organizational Transformation and Change Leadership

  • Champion the firm’s learning and capability transformation strategy, driving adoption of new operating models, workflows, governance, and technologies while challenging legacy approaches that no longer create sufficient value.
  • Lead complex change efforts requiring alignment across service lines, Talent, Learning Operations, Talent Technology, and other shared services, balancing immediate business needs with long-term capability building.
  • Identify barriers to transformation, develop mitigation strategies, and build stakeholder readiness for change.

Portfolio and Investment Leadership

  • Own the strategic portfolio of capability investments for the assigned business, ensuring solutions are connected, scalable, aligned with business and career priorities, and leveraged across the firm where appropriate.
  • Establish priorities and governance for major initiatives, including sponsorship, measures, dependencies, decision rights, and escalation paths.
  • Oversee the business partner budget and recommend resource and investment trade-offs based on expected impact and enterprise priorities.

Solution Leadership and Cross-Functional Partnership

  • Define business problems, target audiences, desired performance, success measures, and constraints before solution design begins.
  • Mobilize and guide cross-functional teams across learning strategy, design, delivery, operations, technology, communications, change, and external partners.
  • Communicate strategy, progress, decisions, risks, and required actions clearly to stakeholders at all levels.

Measurement, Impact, and Continuous Improvement

  • Define meaningful measures that connect capability investments to business, talent, learner, adoption, and performance outcomes.
  • Use data and stakeholder insights to evaluate impact and advise leaders on risks, trade-offs, improvement opportunities, and whether solutions should continue, expand, evolve, or retire.
  • Champion responsible experimentation and adoption of new methods and technologies that improve access, speed, quality, personalization, and impact, and scale leading practices across L&D and Talent.

Enterprise and L&D Leadership

  • Serve as a key member of the L&D leadership team, contributing to enterprise strategy, priorities, governance, and organizational performance.
  • Lead or sponsor enterprise initiatives requiring coordination across businesses, functions, or geographies.
  • Champion modernization through stronger capability consulting, integrated workflows, meaningful measurement, and effective use of technology.
  • Balance business and enterprise priorities, challenge siloed approaches, and facilitate timely decisions with senior stakeholders.
  • Model RSM’s 5 C behaviors by being caring, collaborative, courageous, curious, and an exemplary critical thinker.

People Leadership

  • Build and develop a high-performing, inclusive team of learning professionals focused on business outcomes.
  • Serve as a performance advisor to Managers and/or Associate Directors based on business need and organizational design.
  • Delegate meaningful work, provide timely feedback, address performance gaps, and support career development and succession.
  • Strengthen the team’s business acumen, consulting capability, learning expertise, change leadership, and data fluency while fostering collaboration, continuous learning, thoughtful challenge, and responsible innovation.

Required Qualifications

Education and Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent relevant experience required; advanced degree in learning, organizational development, business, talent management, or a related field preferred.
  • Typically 12+ years of overall experience, with significant relevant experience in learning and development, capability building, performance consulting, organizational effectiveness, talent, or a related discipline. Relevant scope, complexity, and demonstrated impact are more important than tenure alone.
  • Demonstrated success developing strategies that impact business performance and leading large-scale, complex, global, or enterprise-wide initiatives.
  • Experience influencing senior leaders, managing key internal client relationships, and navigating sensitive or high-impact business matters.
  • Experience leading professional teams and serving as a performance advisor to experienced people leaders.
  • Experience in professional services, public accounting, consulting, or another complex, regulated, or knowledge-intensive environment preferred.
  • Knowledge of Assurance, Tax, Consulting, or Firm Client Service business models preferred; CPA or other relevant professional certification is a plus.

Business, Consulting, and Leadership Capabilities

  • Strategic and systems thinking with the ability to connect business strategy, workforce needs, talent practices, and capability investments.
  • Executive-level consulting, influence, facilitation, and communication skills, including the ability to challenge assumptions and recommend trade-offs.
  • Deep knowledge of adult learning, performance consulting, capability development, instructional design, assessment, transfer of learning, and evaluation.
  • Ability to use qualitative and quantitative data to diagnose needs, establish measures, and communicate business impact.
  • Ability to lead through ambiguity, manage risk, resolve complex issues, and align stakeholders across organizational boundaries.
  • Financial and portfolio management experience, including budgeting, investment prioritization, resource decisions, and vendor oversight.
  • Working knowledge of learning technology, digital learning, performance support, knowledge enablement, and emerging approaches to capability development.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft PowerPoint, Word, Excel, SharePoint, and other tools used to analyze, communicate, and manage strategic work.

Success in This Role

  • Business leaders view L&D as a trusted advisor and engage the Director early in strategic workforce and capability decisions.
  • Capability investments are clearly prioritized, connected to business needs, and demonstrate meaningful measures of adoption, performance, and business impact.
  • L&D expertise and effective solutions are mobilized and scaled across the enterprise while distinct business needs are thoughtfully addressed.
  • The Director develops strong leaders and teams and contributes meaningfully to the modernization and impact of L&D.
